items.title: OpenAD5X
items.text:
Open-source software for the FlashForge AD5X.

Kalico (Klipper) on the printer and on all of its boards, the IFS four-colour feeder run by AFC, and Fluidd and GrumpyScreen, all on the hardware you already own. Every part is open source and can be changed.

Get started Discord How we're different

items.title: Why OpenAD5X?
items.text:
• Kalico on the printer

    Kalico runs on the AD5X's own computer and on the mainboard, toolhead board and IFS. Input shaper with the built-in accelerometer, bed probing with the load cell and an adaptive mesh switch.

  • The IFS through AFC

    The four-lane IFS runs as an AFC unit, matched to the stock firmware: selector, feeding, cutting, the purge chute, wipes, auto-load and unload. How the IFS works

  • Fluidd and GrumpyScreen

    Full web control with Fluidd, and GrumpyScreen on the touchscreen. Timelapse, SFTP and root login come with it.

  • Open and editable

    Plain Klipper configs, updates through the Moonraker update panel, and every repository on GitHub.

  • Community

    Developers and owners in one place, for help, testing and what's next. Join the Discord

Development software

Don't treat OpenAD5X as complete. What you've seen from reviews, videos, or anything outside of this wiki may be out of date, different, or not working.

Not sure? Is OpenAD5X for you? walks through what you gain and what you give up. The feature list and status and roadmap show what's finished and what's still in testing.

items.title: Contributing documentation
items.text:
Edit pages under docs/ and add new pages to nav in mkdocs.yml. For hardware instructions, say which printer, firmware version and source commit they're for, and how they were tested. Say plainly when something hasn't been tested.

Use clear language, and only go into technical detail on pages where it's expected.

Before proposing a change, build the site with warnings treated as errors:

.venv/bin/python -m zensical build --strict

On Windows, use .venv\Scripts\python.exe. Install the build tool into .venv with pip install -r docs/requirements.txt. The generated site/ directory is not committed; only the source Markdown and configuration are.

items.title: Videos and other raw HTML
items.text: Markdown images and links work with relative paths. Paths inside raw HTML, such as <video> or <source src="...">, don't: the site loads pages without a full reload, and a relative src is then resolved against the page you came from. Give media in raw HTML its full URL, for example https://openad5x.github.io/assets/videos/<file>.mp4.

items.title: Kalico, not FlashForge's Klipper
items.text: Stock runs an old Klipper on Python 3.8, driven by FlashForge's closed firmwareExe. OpenAD5X runs Kalico, a Klipper fork with more features, on the printer's computer and on every board, including the IFS.

items.title: The IFS, decoded from stock
items.text: The IFS's behaviour was read out of FlashForge's own firmware, move by move: the cut, the purge chute, the wipes, feeding, auto-load and unload. OpenAD5X runs it through AFC and matches it. The details are under IFS.

items.title: Mainstream UIs
items.text: Fluidd, Mainsail and Moonraker come straight from their projects, not forked, so they update as soon as updates come out.

items.title: Full installer
items.text: Pick what you want before it installs: SoC or tunnelled, Fluidd or Mainsail, GrumpyScreen or not. The installer can back up the printer first, and roll back to FlashForge's software from the same USB drive.

items.title: Updates that keep your edits
items.text: Config updates are merged into your files instead of overwriting them, and new MCU firmware is flashed to the boards by itself, like stock.

items.title: Maintainable source
items.text: The code is split by job across the repositories and is plain to read, so it's easy to see what OpenAD5X does.

items.title: Support over Discord
items.text: Feedback and support happen in one place, the Discord.

items.title: OpenAD5X features
items.text:
Finished works on a printer   Testing in testing or untested

Feature Implementation Description Kalico everywhere Finished Kalico on the printer's computer and on the mainboard, toolhead board and IFS. The installer flashes the boards. IFS through AFC Finished The four-lane IFS as an AFC unit: lane select, feeding, the stock cut, purge chute and wipes, load and unload. Tool commands T0 to T3. IFS auto-load Finished Insert a spool and it feeds to the toolhead sensor and parks, as stock. Unload at print end Testing Unloads at the end or cancel of a print; the end_unload switch turns it off. Load cell probing Finished The bed load cell homes Z and probes the bed mesh, with a tare before every probe as stock. Adaptive mesh switch Finished Mesh only where the print is, or the full bed; see How to toggle features. Input shaper and PID in one go Finished ADX_QUICK_START runs input shaper with the built-in accelerometer, nozzle and bed PID, then saves. Stock-style pause and resume Finished Pause parks at the chute; resume heats back up, flushes and brushes like stock. Pause at a layer Finished SET_PAUSE_NEXT_LAYER and SET_PAUSE_AT_LAYER, and Fluidd's and Mainsail's layer pause. Full WebUI support Finished Fluidd or Mainsail with Moonraker; the touchscreen is optional. GrumpyScreen Finished Touchscreen UI with extrude, retract, load and jog; the backlight turns off when it sleeps. Timelapse Finished Moonraker Timelapse, installed by the installer. SFTP over SSH Finished Transfer and manage files with SFTP. Config updates that keep your edits Testing The update merges the new config templates into your files; clashing edits are left in a .conflict file. MCU firmware updates Testing A new MCU firmware version in an update is flashed to the boards by itself, like stock.

items.title: Getting started
items.text:
OpenAD5X replaces FlashForge's software on the AD5X with Kalico, Moonraker, Fluidd and GrumpyScreen, and runs the IFS through AFC. It's in public alpha: see Installation and safety before you install.

Not sure it's for you? Read Is OpenAD5X for you? first.

If you are contributing, start with Project layout and Architecture. The printer configuration lives in AD5X-FS/fs/usr/data/config, while Kalico, the AD5X MCU code and the AFC modules live in kalico-ad5x.

Join our Discord for support and to report problems with the alpha.

items.title: Before installing on a printer
items.text:
• Read Status and roadmap
  • Read Installation and safety
  • Know how to go back to stock
  • Have a USB drive that meets the requirements
  • Join the Discord for support

items.title: Installation and safety
items.text:
OpenAD5X is in public alpha.

Alpha

This is an alpha. Expect bugs, keep a backup, and know how to go back to stock. Report problems on the Discord.

OpenAD5X is installed with the OpenCreator Installer, a touchscreen app that runs from a USB drive and can back up the printer before changing anything. How it works inside is in Installer internals.

items.title: Supported FlashForge firmware
items.text: The installer accepts AD5X printers with FlashForge's kernel package 2.0.1. On any other kernel package it stops without changing anything.

items.title: Requirements for USB
items.text:
• FAT32 partition
  • Room for the backup, if you choose one

items.title: Requirements for printer
items.text:
• At least 256 MB free on /usr/data (the installer warns below that)
  • An active internet connection: the installer downloads Kalico, the AD5X files and the web UI during the install

items.title: Steps to install OpenAD5X
items.text:
1. Copy the installer files to the root of the USB drive. There is no published release yet: the files are built from the touchscreen-installer repository, branch ad5x, with make usb (they end up in dist/usb).
  2. Reboot the printer with the USB drive plugged in.
  3. Go through the steps on the touchscreen. SoC installs are recommended for people who don't know what tunnelled is. Pick Fluidd (recommended) or Mainsail, and whether to install GrumpyScreen.
  4. Wait for the install to finish. It ends by flashing the printer's mainboard, toolhead board and IFS with Kalico.
  5. When it's finished, remove the USB drive and reboot.
  6. After the reboot you should see the OpenAD5X boot logo, GrumpyScreen on the touchscreen, and Fluidd in a browser at the printer's IP address.
  7. Set up your slicer: follow Slicer configuration before your first print.
  8. Run ADX_QUICK_START once (Calibration group in Fluidd's macros): input shaper, nozzle PID and bed PID, then it saves and restarts Klipper.

items.title: Steps to update OpenAD5X
items.text: There are two ways.

items.title: Way 1: Fluidd/Mainsail
items.text:
1. Open the software update section.
  2. Update openad5x, then klipper.
  3. Restart Klipper, or reboot.

Your edits to the config files are kept: the updater merges the new templates into your files. If your edit and the update change the same lines, it leaves a .conflict file next to yours to sort out by hand.

items.title: Way 2: OpenCreator Installer
items.text: For bigger updates, copy the new installer files over the old ones on the USB drive, plug it in and reboot, then follow the steps on the touchscreen.

items.title: Uninstalling OpenAD5X
items.text:
Boot the installer from the USB drive. It offers:

  • Rollback to stock: puts FlashForge's firmwareExe back, so the printer boots FlashForge's software again. OpenAD5X's files stay on the printer for a reinstall.
  • Restore backup: restores the newest backup the installer made.

Files left over

After a rollback these stay on the printer and can be removed by hand: /usr/data/openad5x, /usr/data/grumpyscreen and /usr/data/python-hf. The OpenAD5X boot logo also stays until you restore a backup.

MCU firmware

The install flashes Kalico onto the mainboard, toolhead board and IFS. A rollback puts FlashForge's software back but not FlashForge's MCU firmware.

items.title: AD5X installer
items.text:
The AD5X installs through the OpenCreator installer (touchscreen-installer, branch ad5x), as per-machine branches in the shared scripts ("if C5 then ..., if AD5X then ..."), not as separate AD5X copies. Every AD5X-only step is guarded by OC_MACHINE=AD5X, and the C5 paths are unchanged.

Status

The full install has been run from the USB stick on the test printer (2026-11-03).

items.title: Repos
items.text: Repo AD5X work touchscreen-installer (branch ad5x) Model detection (AD5X, PID 0026), the AD5X boot hook (flashforge_init.sh), and the per-machine install steps below AD5X-FS What the installer copies onto the printer: fs/usr/data/config/, fs/usr/data/openad5x/ (boot, nginx config, flash tools) and mcu-firmware/ad5x/. The installer clones it and keeps the clone as /usr/data/openad5x/ad5x-fs kalico-ad5x Kalico with the AD5X MCU support, the half-duplex RS485 IFS, and the AFC modules, AFC_IFS.py and ad5x_filament_sensor.py in klippy/extras

items.title: Where files go
items.text: OC_HOME is /usr/data/openad5x on the AD5X and /usr/data/opencreator on the C5. It is set in payload-template/common/install-helpers.sh, and in scripts/install.sh (which needs it before it knows the machine, so it reads MACHINE= from the stock app_startup.sh).

items.title: The steps (SoC mode)
items.text:
Step What it does on the AD5X 01-install-entware Entware on /usr/data/bin/opt, mounted on /opt. The legacy-NaN switch is set at 0x00a130d1 (kernel package 2.0.1) 02-install-loopscript Clones AD5X-FS and copies startup, firmware, moonraker, fluidd, plugin-manager, mcu-flash, loadcell, nginx and grumpyscreen from it into /usr/data/openad5x, keeping files you added 05-install-python The hard-float Python 3.13 in /usr/data/python-hf: the Creator 5 bundle, from the AD5X-FS release python-hf-3.13-r1 10-install-stack Kalico (kalico-ad5x) into /usr/data/openad5x/klipper/klipper, a klippy-env, and the default AD5X-FS config into …/klipper/config 15-install-moonraker Arksine's Moonraker into /usr/prog/moonraker, with an environment on python-hf 17-install-timelapse Moonraker timelapse 20-install-web Fluidd (or Mainsail) into /usr/data/fluidd, and Entware's nginx-ssl with the config in /usr/data/openad5x/nginx/nginx.conf (the AD5X has no nginx). Adds a Moonraker update entry for AD5X-FS 30-install-grumpyscreen The latest FlashForge-C5-Modding-Group/grumpyscreen release, when the touchscreen is chosen, and a Moonraker update entry for it 85-enable-root, 86-enable-sftp Root login and SFTP (the 06-sftp.sh boot script patches dropbear) 90-activate-loopscript Replaces firmwareExe with the firmwareExe script, keeping the stock binary as firmwareExe.stock 95-flash-mcu-firmware Flashes mcu-firmware/ad5x with ad5x-mcu-flash; see Flashing

The boot these steps install is described in Startup.

items.title: MCU firmware
items.text: The earlier plan built a stock-format update package (ad5x-update-creator) and let FlashForge's own updater flash it after two power cycles. That path was dropped. The stock app_startup.sh (3.1.5 and 3.1.6, read here) only reads AD5X-*.tgz from a mounted USB stick, and nothing else found picks up a package staged in /usr/data. The installer flashes the repo images directly instead, as the C5 installer does.

items.title: Still open
items.text: • Installer UI (src/) review for machine naming

items.title: USB launcher: AD5X hardware bring-up findings (2026-10-25)
items.text:
The stick was tested on the real AD5X (12 boots). Every fix lives in touchscreen-installer scripts/runFirmwareExe.sh (shipped on the stick as both runFirmwareExe.sh and flashforge_init.sh, the AD5X's hook name):

  • AD5X hook: stock app_startup.sh runs /mnt/flashforge_init.sh (not the C5's runFirmwareExe.sh) and always continues the boot after it returns
  • ethernet: openad5x-style config from Adventurer5M.json; udhcpc must run in the foreground (-n -q -t 5), backgrounded it silently never configured
  • kill dhcpcd first: init starts one that keeps rewriting resolv.conf empty (stock kills it in app_startup.sh only after the hook)
  • real MAC before DHCP: the driver boots with a random MAC and stock sets the real one (/usr/prog/MAC) only later; the interface must be downed to set it
  • public DNS fallbacks appended to resolv.conf after DHCP
  • touch mapping: the installer app has no calibration and trusts the driver's pixels, so the tsc2007 insmod carries the raw-to-pixel actrue window (X 309-3765, Y 705-3447, derived from FlashForge's shipped pointercal); stock's 0-4096 window compresses touch toward the centre
  • rdate/"clock not set" was a DNS casualty, not port 37
  • space gate: /usr/data is 5.5 GB; stock has ~5 GB free and passes the 2 GB check easily (this printer's 1.3 GB free is 3 GB of gcodes)

items.title: Is OpenAD5X for you?
items.text: OpenAD5X replaces FlashForge's software on the AD5X with Kalico, Moonraker and a web UI. It's in public alpha, so it suits some people more than others.

items.title: You'll like OpenAD5X if you
items.text:
• Want a full web UI

    Fluidd or Mainsail with Moonraker, straight from the mainstream projects. You don't need the touchscreen at all.

  • Like to tune and tinker

    Kalico, input shaper with the built-in accelerometer, load cell probing, an adaptive mesh switch and plain Klipper configs. See Features.

  • Want the IFS in Klipper

    The four-lane IFS runs as an AFC unit, with the stock cut, purge chute, wipes, auto-load and unload. See IFS.

  • Want FlashForge's software gone

    FlashForge's firmwareExe no longer runs; Kalico, Moonraker and GrumpyScreen do its job.

items.title: OpenAD5X may not be for you yet if you
items.text:
• Rely on the stock touchscreen. GrumpyScreen replaces it fully, with a new UI.
  • Use FlashForge's app or cloud. These go away with FlashForge's software.
  • Care about your warranty. Installing mods may void it.
  • Want official support. You can't ask FlashForge for software support if you're on custom firmware.
  • Have zero prior experience with 3D printing. You're expected to have at least a basic understanding of Klipper.

items.title: Not sure?
items.text: Check Status and roadmap for what's finished. If OpenAD5X sounds right, head to Getting started, and ask in the Discord if you have questions.

items.title: OpenAD5X
items.text:
OpenAD5X makes the AD5X's host software, MCU firmware, IFS and configuration maintainable as one community-developed stack, for more features and more open software than stock. It's in public alpha; see Installation and safety.

The work is split between kalico-ad5x for Kalico, the AD5X MCU code and the AFC modules, AD5X-FS for the printer files, configuration and boot, and the touchscreen-installer (branch ad5x) for installing. It follows OpenCreator for the Creator 5 where the printers allow; see Differences from OpenCreator.

items.title: What it aims to support
items.text:
Area Goal Status Base software Kalico on the host and on the mainboard, toolhead board and IFS. Finished IFS Run the four-lane IFS as an AFC unit, matched to the stock firmware. Finished Installation and updates Install from USB; update from Fluidd or Mainsail with config merging. Testing Web and touchscreen Fluidd or Mainsail, and GrumpyScreen on the touchscreen. Finished

For what's finished and what's still open in detail, see Status and roadmap and Features.

items.title: Project layout
items.text:
OpenAD5X is split over a few repositories in the FlashForge-C5-Modding-Group organisation. The AD5X ones mirror the Creator 5 project's:

Creator 5 AD5X What it holds OpenCreator openad5x (this repository) The documentation site opencreator-fs AD5X-FS The files that go on the printer: configs, boot, MCU firmware images klipper-c5 / kalico kalico-ad5x Kalico with the AD5X MCU support, the IFS and the AFC modules it uses touchscreen-installer touchscreen-installer (branch ad5x) The installer run from the printer's touchscreen grumpyscreen grumpyscreen GrumpyScreen, the same release as the Creator 5 creator-5-update-creator ad5x-update-creator Builds the update package (no longer used; the installer flashes the repo images)

items.title: What AD5X-FS holds
items.text:
• fs/usr/data/config/: printer.base.cfg, printer.cfg, moonraker.conf, macros.cfg (homing, print start and end, stock AD5X pause and resume, load cell and probe, touchscreen buttons, pause at layer), and AFC/ with AFC.cfg, AFC_Hardware-IFS.cfg, AFC_Macro_Vars.cfg and ifs_macros.cfg
  • fs/usr/data/openad5x/mcu-flash/: ad5x-mcu-flash (flashes the mainboard and IFS live from a folder of mcu-firmware/ad5x images, and stages the eboard for the next power cycle), and ifs_capture.py and ifs_catch.py, which it uses to flash the IFS MCU over its serial port
  • fs/usr/data/openad5x/loadcell/loadcell.sh: bed load cell commands used by macros.cfg
  • fs/usr/data/openad5x/grumpyscreen/grumpyscreen.cfg: the GrumpyScreen config, with your own changes in grumpyscreen.ini in the config folder
  • mcu-firmware/ad5x/: the AD5X MCU firmware images, with the Kalico build configs for the eboard, mainboard and IFS in config/
  • fs/usr/data/openad5x/firmware/firmwareExe, startup/ and version.txt: the boot. firmwareExe brings the network up and runs startup/startup.sh, which starts the scripts in startup/scripts/. See Startup
  • fs/usr/data/openad5x/nginx/nginx.conf: the nginx config (Fluidd and the Moonraker proxy)
  • fs/usr/data/openad5x/startup/commands/: the commands GrumpyScreen runs (restart Klipper, the screen or Wi-Fi, support zip)

items.title: Slicer configuration for OrcaSlicer
items.text: Settings for printing on OpenAD5X from OrcaSlicer, starting from the FlashForge AD5X profile.

items.title: Print profile
items.text:
• Under Others → G-code output, switch Label objects and Exclude objects on.

    This lets the adaptive mesh probe only where the print is, and lets you exclude objects from Fluidd/Mainsail.

items.title: Connection
items.text:
• Click the Wi-Fi connect button (next to the printer) and change the host type to Moonraker.
  • Remove any serial numbers or API keys.

items.title: Printer settings
items.text:
• Printer Agent: switch to Moonraker.
  • Use 3MF instead of G-code: switch off.

items.title: Machine G-code
items.text:
• Machine start G-code: set it to this:
SET_PRINT_STATS_INFO TOTAL_LAYER=[total_layer_count]
START_PRINT EXTRUDER_TEMP=[nozzle_temperature_initial_layer] BED_TEMP=[bed_temperature_initial_layer_single]
G0 Y219.6
G1 X130 E5

START_PRINT heats, homes, probes the mesh and waits at X20 Y219.6, Z0.3; the last two lines draw the prime line along the back edge.

  • Machine end G-code: set it to END_PRINT.

    It unloads the filament (unless the end_unload switch is off), turns the heaters off, lifts the nozzle and parks.

  • Change filament G-code: set it to T[next_extruder].

    AFC runs the IFS colour change for T0 to T3.

  • Layer change G-code: add SET_PRINT_STATS_INFO CURRENT_LAYER={layer_num + 1}.

    Fluidd's and Mainsail's layer pause and SET_PAUSE_AT_LAYER need it.

  • Layer change G-code (optional, for timelapses): add TIMELAPSE_TAKE_FRAME on its own line, so timelapse takes a frame at every layer.

items.text: A few OpenAD5X features are switches you can turn on or off.

FluiddMainsailConsole

items.title: Switches
items.text: Switch Default What it does Adaptive_Mesh On On: START_PRINT probes the mesh only where the print is. Off: the full bed. end_unload On Unloads the filament at the end or cancel of a print. The setting survives restarts.

items.title: Architecture
items.text:
OpenAD5X replaces FlashForge's closed programs on the AD5X with open-source ones. FlashForge's Linux stays as it is: there is no custom distribution.

The closed program being replaced is firmwareExe (/usr/prog/PROGRAM/software/). It is the screen app, but it also runs most of the printer.

The end goal is one OS for all FlashForge printers, so the layout follows OpenCreator (the Creator 5 project) wherever the printers allow. See Differences from OpenCreator.

items.title: What firmwareExe does
items.text: Taken from firmwareExe 3.1.0.

items.title: Must be replaced
items.text:
The printer does not work without these.

# Job 1 Starts Klipper at boot (/usr/prog/klipper/start.sh) 2 Wakes the toolhead board at power-on (sends A on /dev/ttyS5) 3 Runs printing: start, pause, resume and cancel, through Klipper's API socket 4 Network: brings up eth0 and Wi-Fi, saves Wi-Fi networks, hotspot mode 5 Power button and safe power-off 6 Touchscreen: all menus and screen sleep

items.title: Replace if used
items.text: # Job 7 IFS 4-colour unit (/dev/ttyS4): load, unload, colour change, cut, purge 8 Load cell weighing and crash detection (/dev/ttyS7) 9 Camera stream (mjpg_streamer, port 8080) 10 USB stick detection and printing 11 Buzzer sounds 12 Clock from the internet (ntpclient)

items.title: FlashForge-only, dropped
items.text: # Job 13 FlashForge cloud (MQTT, Alibaba OSS uploads) 14 FlashPrint and Orca network printing (Moonraker covers normal slicers) 15 FlashForge update system 16 FlashForge calibration and setup wizards

items.title: What stock does
items.text: firmwareExe has its own streamer built in, using mjpg-streamer code: V4L2 capture, GET /?action=stream, Server: MJPG-Streamer/0.2, port 8080 and camera hot-plug. Its command line for an external /usr/prog/mjpg-streamer/bin/mjpg_streamer is dead code: that program is in no AD5X package (factory image, 3.1.0 update, rootfs, 3.1.5, 3.1.6). With firmwareExe stopped there is no camera until one is started.

items.title: FlashForge's mjpg-streamer
items.text:
FlashForge ships mjpg-streamer.zip separately. It was built with Ingenic XBurst2 GCC 7.2.0 and glibc 2.29, has flags 0x70001405 (the same as firmwareExe) and its own libjpeg 9e, and uses the printer's libc, libdl and libpthread.

It is installed unchanged at /usr/prog/mjpg-streamer (files 644, directories, binaries and .so files 755). Its start_webcam.sh and .orig are not used; it is unknown which one is stock, and the .orig needs v4l2-ctl, which the printer does not have.

items.title: The drop-in
items.text:
startup/scripts/30-camera.sh runs firmwareExe's own command without the cloud snapshot output file:

LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/usr/prog/mjpg-streamer mjpg_streamer \
  -i "input_uvc.so -d <camera> -r 1280x720 -f 30" \
  -o "output_http.so -w /usr/prog/mjpg-streamer/www --port 8080"
  • Finding the camera: it scans /sys/class/video4linux for the uvcvideo driver at index 0 (index 1 is metadata). It skips video2, which is the X2600's decoder (felix-vdec).
  • Hot-plug: it waits for a camera and starts again after an unplug (a 5 s loop).
  • Log: /usr/data/logs/mjpg-streamer.log. The UVCIOC_CTRL_ADD/MAP "Inappropriate ioctl" lines are harmless (Logitech extension controls).
  • Kernel: uvcvideo is built in. The tested camera is a Logitech Brio 101.

items.title: Web
items.text:
nginx passes /webcam/ to 127.0.0.1:8080. moonraker.conf has a [webcam printer] section (mjpegstreamer, /webcam/?action=stream, /webcam/?action=snapshot), so Fluidd shows the stream.

Tested on 2026-10-18: Fluidd shows the camera, and after a power cycle 30-camera started at boot, the camera was /dev/video0 and port 8080 was up.

An own ustreamer build (ustreamer-ff) is on hold and not used.

items.title: Entware and Python
items.text:
Kalico builds c_helper.so on the printer, so the printer needs a compiler and a recent Python. Entware provides gcc, and a hard-float Python 3.13 provides the interpreter. The method is the same as the one in the Creator 5 group's touchscreen-installer (common/install-entware.sh).

CPU: Ingenic XBurst II, isa mips32r2 and mips32r5, MSA.

items.title: Entware
items.text:
Installed on 2026-10-23.

busybox devmem 0x00a130d1 8 1        # legacy NaN byte (kernel package 2.0.1)
mkdir -p /usr/data/bin/opt
mount --bind /usr/data/bin/opt /opt
wget -O - http://bin.entware.net/mipselsf-k3.4/installer/generic.sh | sh
/opt/bin/opkg install gcc            # OpenWrt GCC 8.4.0, about 35 MB
wget -O - http://bin.entware.net/mipselsf-k3.4/include/include.tar.gz | gunzip -c | tar x -C /opt/include
  • The mipselsf-k3.4 packages are glibc 2.27 (loader ld.so.1). The printer has glibc 2.33.
  • /usr/data free space: 2.2 GB before, 1.7 GB after.
  • Packages: gcc 8.4.0-8, libgcc 8.4.0-12, binutils 2.45.1-1, libc 2.27-12.
  • gcc --version also prints "unrecognized command line option" for -msoft-float -mllsc -mno-shared -mabi=32 and exits 0.
  • gcc needs /opt/bin on PATH, because it runs as and ld from there.

items.title: The empty specs file
items.text:
The gcc install leaves /opt/lib/gcc/mipsel-openwrt-linux-gnu/8.4.0/specs as a 0-byte file (-rw-------). When a specs file exists, the driver reads it instead of setting up its built-in specs. No spec then claims any option, so every option (-O2, -g, -Wall, even its own -msoft-float -mllsc -mno-shared) is "unrecognized" and nothing compiles. cc1 and Entware's libc were fine (strncmp, strcmp and memcmp tested: 0 wrong out of 35376).

Fix: mv specs specs.empty. It is unknown why the install writes it empty. opkg install --force-reinstall gcc recreates it, so check after any gcc reinstall or upgrade.

items.title: Test
items.text: Plain gcc -O2 -Wall -g -c works. Through the python-hf wrapper (PATH=/usr/data/python-hf/cc/bin:$PATH:/opt/bin), gcc -Wall -g -O2 -shared -fPIC builds a .so with flags 0x70001407 (nan2008, mips32r2, FP ABI hard float 64-bit FPU), needing libpthread, libc and libm, with RPATH /usr/data/python-hf/lib:/opt/lib. A Python 3.13 cffi dlopen and call works.

items.title: Python 3.13
items.text:
Installed on 2026-10-23 at /usr/data/python-hf from the opencreator-fs release python-3.13-hardfloat-r2, file python-hf-c5.tar.gz (sha256 30989fdb8cc353691574c21d75af33287e8b164d043c0a32ed87dc58637bc3dc, checked on the printer).

  • The tarball was copied with pscp -scp (the printer has no sftp-server) and unpacked with gunzip -c | tar x (busybox tar has no z).
  • Python 3.13.9 runs, and cffi, greenlet, jinja2, markupsafe, numpy and serial import. markupsafe has no package metadata (markupsafe.__version__ fails), which Klippy does not need.
  • cc/bin/gcc is a wrapper for Kalico's c_helper.so build. It calls /opt/bin/gcc with -mips32r2 -mhard-float -mfp64 -mnan=2008 and its own glibc headers and crt files. This works since the specs fix. Klippy needs PATH=/usr/data/python-hf/cc/bin:$PATH:/opt/bin to build c_helper.so.

items.title: c_helper.so test
items.text: The kalico-ad5x klippy/chelper folder, copied to /tmp/chelper-test, with chelper.get_ffi() under python-hf and that PATH: it builds c_helper.so in about 46 s (305 KB, 0x70001407 nan2008 mips32r2, FP ABI hard float 64-bit FPU), loads, and trapq_alloc() and trapq_free() work.

items.title: At boot
items.text:
01-fixnan.sh sets the NaN byte and 05-entfix.sh bind-mounts /opt and runs /opt/etc/init.d/rc.unslung start (the previous boot's startup.d/05-entware.sh did both). A power-cycle test with the previous boot passed on 2026-10-23: /opt was mounted, gcc was there, and the NaN byte was 0x01.

The NaN byte is needed again because the old 10-nan-relaxed.sh was dropped on 2026-10-17 (GrumpyScreen from grumpy-ff does not need it), but Entware's binaries do. The byte and the bind mount are lost on reboot, which is why a boot script sets them.

items.title: Network
items.text:
How the stock firmware brings up the network. Settings are the network section of /usr/prog/config/Adventurer5M.json, and saved Wi-Fi networks are in /usr/prog/wifi/wpa_supplicant.conf.

Only one mode is active. They are checked in this order at boot:

Mode Stock function What it runs Hotspot wifiHotspotStatus ifconfig wlan0 up, ifconfig wlan0 192.168.0.240, udhcpd -I 192.168.0.240, hostapd -B /usr/prog/wifi/rtl_hostapd_2G.conf Wi-Fi wifiStationStatus wpa_supplicant -d -Dnl80211 -iwlan0 -c/usr/prog/wifi/wpa_supplicant.conf -B, then wpa_cli -i wlan0 enable_network all, then an address on wlan0 Ethernet ethernetStatus ifconfig eth0 up. The cable state is /sys/class/net/eth0/carrier. Then an address on eth0

items.title: Getting an address
items.text:
For Wi-Fi and Ethernet:

Setting What runs isUdhcpc udhcpc -i <iface> isManual ifconfig <iface> <configIp> netmask <configNetmask>, route add default gw <configGateway>, and nameserver <configDns> in /etc/resolv.conf

items.title: Cable changes
items.text:
• Ethernet cable plugged in: killall udhcpc, flush the address, DHCP again.
  • Ethernet cable pulled: killall udhcpc, flush the address.

The eth0 MAC address is set earlier by app_startup.sh, from /usr/prog/MAC.

Adding and saving Wi-Fi networks (wpa_cli add_network, save_config) is a job for the touchscreen menu, not for startup.

items.title: SFTP
items.text: Stock dropbear starts /usr/libexec/sftp-server, which the read-only root does not have. 06-sftp.sh copies /usr/sbin/dropbear to /usr/data/openad5x/bin/dropbear-sftp, changes the one /usr/libexec/sftp-server string in the copy to /opt/libexec/sftp-server (Entware's, from openssh-sftp-server; the same length, so the file size stays the same), bind-mounts the copy over /usr/sbin/dropbear and restarts S50dropbear. It waits for /opt to be mounted, and does nothing if the string is not found. The stock AD5X dropbear has that string once, at offset 220360.

items.title: Differences from OpenCreator
items.text:
OpenAD5X follows OpenCreator (Creator 5) where the printers allow, so the two can share work. The boot has the same structure, and these are the differences. It was last compared on 2026-10-30; check the opencreator-fs repository before relying on a row.

Part OpenAD5X OpenCreator Base folder /usr/data/openad5x /usr/data/opencreator firmwareExe Network from Adventurer5M.json (hotspot, Wi-Fi, ethernet with a cable watch, static addresses), no coprocessor Wi-Fi watchdog (USB reset) and the SoC coprocessor startup.sh Starts the scripts in parallel The same, and first runs the MCU flash the installer staged in mcu-flash-pending NaN setting 01-fixnan sets the byte for Entware's binaries on kernel 2.0.1 01-fixnan (0x00B330D1 on C5 2.0.7) Clock 02-fixtime (rdate) 02-fixtime (rdate) Entware 05-entfix 05-entfix SFTP 06-sftp patches dropbear the same way 06-sftp Toolhead board wake 08-mcu-wake: the eboard only, started before Klippy, with the eboard.flash hook 08-mcu-wake for the C5's boards, started when Klippy cannot connect Klipper start 10-klipper, with oc-plugin sync for the modules (AFC and the IFS are in kalico-ad5x) 10-klipper, with oc-plugin sync for the modules Moonraker 20-moonraker, installed by the installer (Arksine on python-hf) 20-msmr (and nginx) nginx 25-nginx: Entware's nginx, because the AD5X has none The stock nginx in /usr/prog Camera 30-camera: FlashForge's own mjpg-streamer command 30-camera with the C5 camera settings Touchscreen 40-grumpyscreen, the same GrumpyScreen release, plus a touch driver reload for the AD5X panel 40-grumpyscreen MCU flashing ad5x-mcu-flash: mainboard and IFS live, eboard at the next power cycle The installer flashes the four boards from an update package Updates 99-opencreator-updater, cloning AD5X-FS 99-opencreator-updater, tunneled bridge Plugins plugin-manager plugin-manager

items.title: Worth taking from OpenCreator
items.text:
• The Wi-Fi watchdog (USB reset)
  • power_loss_recovery (from their klipper-c5)

items.title: GrumpyScreen
items.text: OpenAD5X uses the same GrumpyScreen release as OpenCreator. That build has no touch calibration, so 40-grumpyscreen.sh reloads the AD5X touch driver with the panel's touch window. See Touchscreen.

items.title: Packages and builds
items.text:
Moonraker and Fluidd are packaged as two tarballs and built on a PC. The build scripts were in AD5X-FS, under build/, and have been removed.

Previous layout

This is how the test printer got Moonraker and the web UI. The installer no longer uses these tarballs: it clones Arksine's Moonraker into /usr/prog/moonraker with an environment on python-hf, installs Fluidd from its latest release, and uses Entware's nginx-ssl. The packages and their tested details are kept here until the new way has run on a printer.

items.title: Moonraker package (moonraker-ad5x.tar.gz)
items.text:
Moonraker is pinned at commit abd2026b90 and reports version v0.9.3-abd2026. Later commits raise the Python requirements (3ea83163b0, paho-mqtt 2.1.0 and others) beyond what this Python can use.

It runs on FlashForge's Python 3.8.2:

Variable Value PYTHONPATH /usr/data/moonraker-env/site-packages LD_LIBRARY_PATH /usr/data/moonraker-env/lib plus FlashForge's libraries SSL_CERT_FILE the certifi bundle in site-packages

What goes into the package:

  • Pure-Python packages from an existing Moonraker environment built for this ABI (pip, setuptools and virtualenv left out).
  • From the Creality Ender-3 V3 firmware F001_V1.2.3.23, which has the same MIPS NaN2008/FP64 ABI: the sqlite3 package, the _sqlite3 module, libsqlite3.so.0 and libsodium.so.23.
  • From FlashForge's Python: lmdb, pillow 7.0.0, streaming-form-data 1.8.1 and pyserial.

moonraker.conf has no [update_manager]: Moonraker must not update itself.

items.title: Web package (fluidd-ad5x.tar.gz)
items.text:
nginx 1.17.7 comes from the same Ender-3 V3 firmware. It needs libpcre.so.1 and libz.so.1, which are both on the AD5X.

Port 80 serves /usr/data/fluidd and passes /websocket, /printer, /api, /access, /machine and /server to Moonraker. There is a harmless startup alert: nginx tries its built-in /var/log/nginx/error.log before it reads nginx.conf.

items.title: Build inputs
items.text:
Where the outside parts of each build come from:

Input Source Moonraker source https://codeload.github.com/Arksine/moonraker/tar.gz/<MR_COMMIT in build.py> Moonraker environment (pure-Python packages) Simple AF's k1/moonraker-env.tar.gz sqlite3, libsodium, nginx, mime.types F001_V1.2.3.23.ingenic, file images/rootfs.squashfs (unpacked with 7-Zip) Fluidd A Fluidd release (v1.37.6 used) GrumpyScreen The FlashForge-C5-Modding-Group/grumpyscreen release

items.title: Building the packages
items.text: Downloads and extracted files are not kept in the repository. Put them in a throwaway folder next to a copy of build.py.

items.title: moonraker-ad5x.tar.gz
items.text:
Files needed:

  • <folder>/dl/moonraker.tar.gz (the Moonraker source, from the table above)
  • argument 1: the Moonraker environment archive
  • argument 2: a folder with the files extracted from the F001 rootfs:
    • usr/lib/libsqlite3.so.0.8.6
    • usr/lib/libsodium.so.23.3.0
    • usr/lib/python3.8/sqlite3/*.py
    • usr/lib/python3.8/lib-dynload/_sqlite3.cpython-38-mipsel-linux-gnu.so
python build.py <moonraker-env.tar.gz> <f001 folder>

items.title: fluidd-ad5x.tar.gz
items.text:
Files needed:

  • <folder>/nginx.conf
  • <folder>/dl/fluidd.zip (the Fluidd release)
  • argument 1: the same F001 folder, plus usr/sbin/nginx and etc/nginx/mime.types
python build.py <f001 folder>

items.title: Installing
items.text: Stream the tarball to the printer with gunzip -c | tar -xf - -C /usr/data (busybox tar has no -z). Copy moonraker.conf to /usr/data/config/moonraker.conf.

items.title: Power key
items.text:
The AD5X only has a hard power switch, so none of the power-key code is needed. firmwareExe's power-key code is shared with other FlashForge models:

  1. MainWindow::powerKeyChecking finds the input device named md-gpio-keys (keyboard_gpio_add.ko, PB11, KEY_POWER2) and starts PowerKeyThread on it.
  2. A key press calls MainWindow::doPowerOff(): it wakes the screen and asks "Do you want to turn off the printer ?". On Yes it calls gpio_out(44, 0).

Nothing is wired to PB11 on the AD5X, so this never fires.

The same GPIO 44 = 0 is used by the screen's power-off, by power-off after a print (printCompletedPowerOff) and by FlashForge's app (doPowerOff(string,int)). What GPIO 44 does on the AD5X is unknown. Reproducing it is optional and not needed for printing.

items.title: Not needed
items.text: /dev/ttyS3 is unused air-quality sensor code from another model. firmwareExe never starts it.

items.title: Files on the printer
items.text:
The stock baseline is FlashForge AD5X firmware (software 3.1.0, control 1.1.1, kernel 2.0.1, library 2.0.1). Everything below is added or changed on top of it. Console access is by SSH as root.

The layout follows the installer in the touchscreen-installer repository (branch ad5x) and the files in AD5X-FS. It is installed on the test printer (USB stick install, 2026-11-03). The layout it had before is under Previous layout.

The stock binary is kept as /usr/data/openad5x/firmwareExe.stock /usr/data/openad5x/firmware/firmwareExe The source of that script /usr/data/openad5x/startup/startup.sh Starts every script in startup/scripts/ /usr/data/openad5x/startup/scripts/ The boot scripts, see Startup /usr/data/openad5x/startup/commands/ The commands GrumpyScreen runs: restart-klipper.sh, restart-gui.sh, restart-wifi.sh, support-zip.sh

items.title: Toolchain
items.text:
Path What it is /usr/data/bin/opt Entware, bind-mounted on /opt, with gcc, git, git-http, ca-bundle and nginx-ssl /usr/data/python-hf Python 3.13.9 hard-float

See Entware and Python.

items.title: MCU firmware
items.text:
The mainboard, the eboard and the IFS on the test printer run kalico-ad5x v2026.10.00-161-g8ee87b51, flashed by the installer on 2026-11-03. Before that the mainboard was flashed with NationsCommand, and the eboard with IAPCommand through the startup hook. The stock images are the way back: /usr/prog/PROGRAM/control/1.1.1/AD5X.bin for the mainboard, ADM_App.hex for the eboard. IAPCommand deletes /usr/prog/PROGRAM/control/Update and NationsCommand deletes UpdateM.

The installer flashes the images in mcu-firmware/ad5x with ad5x-mcu-flash; see Flashing.

FlashForge's own Klipper no longer runs with these MCUs (MCU protocol error, config_lis2dw) until the host runs Kalico.

items.title: Previous layout (test printer)
items.text:
The layout the test printer had before the install:

Path What it is /usr/prog/app_startup.sh The firmwareExe start and restart block replaced by a call to startup.sh /usr/prog/openad5x/startup.sh, /usr/data/openad5x/startup.d/ The startup core and its drop-ins /usr/data/kalico/{klipper,klippy-env,start.sh} Kalico, its environment and the loop that keeps Klippy running /usr/data/config/kalico/ The Kalico config, a copy of the stock printer.cfg and printer.base.cfg with max_accel_to_decel replaced by minimum_cruise_ratio: 0.75 /usr/data/logs/klippy.log Kalico log /usr/data/moonraker, /usr/data/moonraker-env Moonraker on FlashForge's Python 3.8 and its packages /usr/data/nginx nginx and nginx.conf /usr/data/ad5x-afc AFC_IFS.py, linked into klippy/extras

items.title: Startup
items.text: How the printer boots with OpenAD5X. The structure follows OpenCreator: a firmwareExe script brings the network up and hands over to startup.sh, which starts a folder of scripts. The files are in AD5X-FS under fs/usr/data/openad5x/.

items.title: The chain
items.text:
1. FlashForge's /usr/prog/app_startup.sh runs the USB hook, the control update check and the drivers, then starts /usr/prog/PROGRAM/software/firmwareExe -1 -D -qws. After 10 s it copies the stock binary back and starts it again unless a process named firmwareExe is running.
  2. The installer replaces that file with the firmwareExe script. The stock binary is kept as /usr/data/openad5x/firmwareExe.stock.
  3. The script sets the legacy NaN byte, mounts Entware if needed, and brings the network up from Adventurer5M.json: hotspot, Wi-Fi or ethernet (with a cable watch), static addresses included. It then runs startup/startup.sh and stays alive in a sleep loop, so app_startup.sh does not restore the stock binary. The network comes first, so SSH still works if a later script breaks.
  4. startup.sh starts every script in /usr/data/openad5x/startup/scripts/ in the background, in name order.

items.title: The scripts
items.text:
Script What it does 01-fixnan.sh Sets the legacy NaN byte for Entware's binaries (0x00a130d1 on kernel package 2.0.1). Called by firmwareExe and 05-entfix.sh 02-fixtime.sh Sets the clock (see below) 05-entfix.sh Bind-mounts Entware on /opt and runs rc.unslung start 06-sftp.sh SFTP for dropbear (see Network) 08-mcu-wake.sh Starts the eboard application, flashing it first when asked, then wakes the eboard again whenever Klippy cannot reach it 10-klipper.sh Creates empty AFC variable files when missing, waits for the eboard, syncs the Klipper plugins (oc-plugin sync) and keeps Klippy running 20-moonraker.sh Moonraker from /usr/prog/moonraker, data folder /usr/data/openad5x/klipper 25-fluidd-macros.sh Once Moonraker is up, gives Fluidd the OpenAD5X macro groups (fluidd/macros.json) if it has no layout yet 25-nginx.sh Entware's nginx, with Fluidd on port 80 30-camera.sh FlashForge's mjpg-streamer on port 8080 40-grumpyscreen.sh GrumpyScreen with DISPLAY_ROTATE=0, the full config openad5x/grumpyscreen/grumpyscreen.cfg and your changes in config/grumpyscreen.ini; at every boot it sets hide_spoolman (from [spoolman] in moonraker.conf) and hide_mmu (from AFC in printer.cfg) in the .ini 99-opencreator-updater.sh Runs opencreator_updater.py, which merges AD5X-FS config updates into the live config and keeps the openad5x folders current (log /tmp/openad5x-updater.log)

The scripts run in parallel, so a script that needs another one waits for it: 10-klipper.sh for the eboard (/tmp/openad5x-eboard-ready, up to 90 s), and 25-nginx.sh and 06-sftp.sh for /opt.

items.title: Eboard start and flash hook
items.text: 08-mcu-wake.sh talks to the eboard bootloader on ttyS5 at 115200 before Klippy connects. It waits for the Ready lines and sends A; the bootloader answers ACK (0x06) and starts the application. If /usr/data/kalico-fw/eboard.flash exists, it holds the path of a .hex to flash first with IAPCommand. The file is deleted once the flash log shows STM32Write: success; after a failure it stays and is tried again at the next power-on (once per boot). The log is /usr/data/logs/openad5x/eboard-flash.log. See Flashing.

items.title: Clock
items.text:
The printer has no battery clock and boots at 1970. 02-fixtime.sh sets it from the network with rdate once time.nist.gov answers a ping, trying up to 30 times 2 seconds apart.

The clock matters because with a 1970 date HTTPS fails with "certificate is not yet valid".

items.title: Web access
items.text: Fluidd is at http://<printer>/ through nginx, and Moonraker is on port 7125.

items.title: Logs
items.text: Log Contents /tmp/openad5x.log firmwareExe, startup.sh and the scripts' launcher messages /tmp/<script>.log Output of each script /usr/data/openad5x/klipper/logs/printer.log Klippy /usr/data/logs/mcu-wake.log, /usr/data/logs/openad5x/eboard-flash.log Eboard wake and flash /usr/data/logs/mcu-flash.log ad5x-mcu-flash /usr/data/logs/nginx-error.log nginx

items.title: Recovery
items.text: If the scripts break, the network and SSH are still up. To go back to the stock firmware, copy /usr/data/openad5x/firmwareExe.stock over /usr/prog/PROGRAM/software/firmwareExe. Keep a copy of the original app_startup.sh (the official file, md5 08ba2971...) off the printer.

items.title: Previous boot
items.text:
Before this, the test printer used one line in app_startup.sh, replacing the firmwareExe block:

/usr/prog/openad5x/startup.sh > /usr/data/logs/openad5x.log 2>&1 &

That startup.sh ran the eboard, Klipper (/usr/data/kalico/start.sh), the network and the clock in a fixed order, then the drop-ins in /usr/data/openad5x/startup.d/ one after another. It is what the power-cycle tests below ran on. Its clock was /usr/prog/ntpclient -c 1 -s -h pool.ntp.org every 5 s until the year was 2024 or later (-c 1 sets the time once and exits; without it ntpclient stays running and re-syncs every 600 s).

items.title: Tested
items.text: On the previous boot, power-cycle tests passed on 2026-10-10 (eboard, Klipper with both MCUs configured, network, Moonraker, nginx), on 2026-10-11 (the clock: set, no ntpclient left running, no certificate errors) and on 2026-10-23 (Entware and gcc).

items.title: Touchscreen
items.text: The touchscreen app is GrumpyScreen, the same release as the Creator 5: FlashForge-C5-Modding-Group/grumpyscreen. The installer's 30-install-grumpyscreen downloads the latest release binary and adds a [update_manager grumpyscreen] entry to moonraker.conf, so it updates from Fluidd.

items.title: On the printer

items.title: History
items.text:
Until November 2026 OpenAD5X used grumpy-ff, a NaN2008 rebuild of the upstream GrumpyScreen release with GUPPY_CALIBRATE, because the upstream release is MIPS32r1, FPXX and legacy NaN. The X2600 kernel (no ieee754= on the command line) refuses it.

The first workarounds, on 2026-10-11, were a one-byte e_flags NaN2008 patch, the kernel NaN byte (busybox devmem 0x00a130d1 8 1 on kernel 2.0.1; on the C5 it is 0x00a130d1 for 2.0.5 and 2.0.6, and 0x00b330d1 for 2.0.7) set by a 10-nan-relaxed.sh drop-in, and a touch-scale change in the tsc2007 values. All of them were dropped once grumpy-ff built a NaN2008 binary. A power-cycle test passed on 2026-10-17 with the NaN byte at 0.

items.title: IFS
items.text:
The IFS is the AD5X's four-lane filament feeder: one selector motor that clamps a lane onto a feed wheel, one feed motor, four filament sensors and four speed sensors. It has its own MCU, a Nations N32G455 board, which talks to the printer over RS485 on /dev/ttyS4.

OpenAD5X runs the IFS with Kalico firmware as a unit of AFC, and matches the stock behaviour decoded from the stock firmware.

items.title: AD5X IFS motor spec (research, 2026-10-25)
items.text: Bottom line: no source found that gives the exact model or electrical ratings of the AD5X IFS motors. Everything electrical below is inferred from the photo (35BYJ46-class) and generic 35BYJ46 listings. Measure the real motor before trusting any number.

items.title: 1. Motor identity
items.text:
Fact Status Source IFS has two separate stepper motors: filament feed (white connector) and channel change/selector (blue connector) Confirmed https://filament2print.com/de/flashforge-ad5x-ersatzteile/3902-motoren-flashforge-ad5x.html ; https://partsbuilt.com/ifs-filament-feeding-motor-for-ad5x-flashforge/ ; https://partsbuilt.com/stepper-motor-for-ifs-channel-changing-ad5x-flashforge/ (titles seen in search only, pages returned 403) Motor type = 35 mm can-stack geared PM stepper, blue molded housing, D-flat shaft Inferred from a photo of the motor; no source names "35BYJ46" for AD5X Model number NOT FOUND Rated voltage NOT FOUND. Generic 35BYJ46 is 12 V typical; variants 5-36 V exist (https://www.micro-steppermotor.com/sale-14494393-35byj46-voltage-pm-stepper-motor-7-5-stepper-motor-5-wire-permanent-magnet-stepper-motor.html ; https://maintexmotors.com/product/35byj46-stepper-motor/ lists 3-24 V) Coil resistance NOT FOUND. Generic: 130 ohm (12 V) and 300 ohm (12 V/24 V) variants; Maintex range 10-600 ohm Rated phase current NOT FOUND. A generic 12 V 130 ohm vendor listing says 100 mA/phase Step angle Inferred: 7.5 deg (rotor) with typical 1/42.5 or 1/85 gearbox -> 3.75 or 15 deg-class output; Maintex lists step angles 3.75/7.5/15 and ratios 1/85, 1/42.5, 1/127. Actual ratio NOT FOUND Wires / connector NOT FOUND. Photo shows several thin wires out of the blue housing; 35BYJ46 are commonly 5-wire unipolar (center tap) or 4-wire. Connector colours: feed = white, selector = blue (confirmed, filament2print) Shaft D-flat (from photo)

Not found anywhere: teardowns, Reddit/Facebook/forum posts, GitHub issues, or AliExpress/Amazon listings naming the AD5X IFS motor model. partsbuilt.com pages blocked fetch (HTTP 403).
