items.title: 2. FFS_state machine (FUN_0801900c, run each TIM6 tick, 78 us)
2.1 Meaning of the state numbers
items.text:
State (dec / hex) Meaning 0 power-up value. Does nothing. Selector NOT homed. F10/F11 reply "not ready" 1 homing start 2 homing back-off (sensor was active at start) 3 homing forward seek 4 homed, dispatch to target slot 5 idle / ready (only state in which F10/F11 are accepted). 6: also no-op (unused) 7 move to slot 1 (count 0); 8, 9 settle, then 5 12 (0x0c) move to neutral at count 2048 (also used for target 0); 13 -> 5 18 (0x12) / 19, 20 move to slot 2 (4096) 23 (0x17) / 24 move to neutral 6144 29 (0x1d) / 30, 31 move to slot 3 (8192) 34 (0x22) / 35 move to neutral 10240 40 (0x28) / 41, 42 move to slot 4 (12288) 45 (0x2d) / 46 move to neutral 14336 F10 feeding ch1: 10 (start, one tick) then 11 (waiting); ch2: 21 then 22; ch3: 32 then 33; ch4: 43 then 44. When the planner queue empties: ch1 -> 13, ch2 -> 24, ch3 -> 35, ch4 -> 46, each -> 5 next tick. Motor enable stays on F11 unloading ch1: 14 (start), 15 (wait), 16 (stop); ch2: 25, 26, 27; ch3: 36, 37, 38; ch4: 47, 48, 49. State "stop" calls FUN_08015d28 (planner reset, PA5 high, PB1 high) then 5 101-120 (0x65-0x78), 121-125 set 0x200001d5[i] = 1 or nothing. No code writes these states: dead 126 (0x7e) homing error: PB1 high, PB6 high, PB5 low (repeated each tick) 127 (0x7f) "driver was reset, re-homed" marker: set at the end of homing when 0x20000098 = 1 (clears it); stays 127 until the host sends F15, F18, F24 or F112 (the stock host sends F15, then repeats the F10/F11) 128 (0x80) / 129 (0x81) F30 manual move; 129 is terminal (never returns to 5 by itself)

The user's guess is confirmed: 11 / 22 / 33 / 44 are the "feeding, waiting for the move to finish" states for channels 1..4. Host feed completion = state back to 5.

items.title: 2.2 Feed F10 (states 10/11 and siblings)
items.text:
• Start state: clears stall counter of that channel (0x2000152c[ch-1] = 0), 0x20000158 = 0, calls FUN_080163bc(L, S): queues ONE move of L mm (sign = direction) at S/60 mm/s on axis 0 (feed motor PA0/PA1/PA5), 343.696 steps/mm, trapezoid planner, accel/min rate in STOCK_MOTOR_DRIVE.md section 3. Then wait state: (wr - rd) & 0x7f == 0 of the planner block queue (FUN_08016374) -> finished. The planner ramps automatically (Marlin-like trapezoid); there is no extra ramp or final stop code in the F10 path. EN (PA5) is left low (motor energised, IHOLD=0), only F112 / F11 end / driver-reset stop release it.
  • The selector is NOT touched by F10/F11: the host must have clamped the channel with F24 first. F10 does not verify the selected channel against C (it feeds whatever lane is clamped).
  • No retry, no stall detection, no timeout in the firmware. L=0 finishes immediately.

items.title: 2.3 Unload F11
items.text: Same, with L negated (the move goes backwards), and ending in the stop state (FUN_08015d28: planner reset + PA5 high + PB1 high, so the selector motor is also released) then state 5. Host retries (F11 C L70 ...) are host logic (STOCK_HOST_RELEASE.md).

items.title: 2.4 Mid-operation changes
items.text:
• F24, F39, F18, F30 and F15 have no state check: they overwrite FFS_state immediately. The feed planner is NOT reset by them (TIM5 keeps stepping the queued move until it ends, EN stays low) and the abandoned feed state never reaches its stop state. Only F112 (when 0x20000098 = 0) or the driver-reset handler resets the planner.
  • F10/F11 while state != 5: refused with "FFS not ready" and no state change.
  • F24 while moving the selector: restarts at state 1 (re-homes from wherever it is).

items.title: 2.5 Selector moves (positions)
items.text:
8 microsteps, one step = STEP (PA7) low tick then high tick; position counter changes on the rising tick; 6410 steps/s = 140.86 deg/s constant, no ramp. 16384 counts = 360 degrees (2048 full steps).

Target State Count Angle slot 1 (home sensor edge) 7 0 0 neutral after slot 1 (target 0, F39 C1) 0x0c 2048 45 slot 2 0x12 4096 90 neutral (F39 C2) 0x17 6144 135 slot 3 0x1d 8192 180 neutral (F39 C3) 0x22 10240 225 slot 4 0x28 12288 270 neutral (F39 C4) 0x2d 14336 315

Per tick in a move state: PB1 (EN) low (enabled). If count == target: PB1 high (EN off), go to the settle states (each one tick, then 5). Else alternate: low phase = PA7 low; high phase = PA7 high and, if count < target: PA6 (DIR) high, flag 0x2000021a = 1, count++; else PA6 low, flag 0, count--. Move takes the shortest direct count difference (no wrap-around, never the long way). The arrival check happens on every tick, so the motor is off (PB1 high) as soon as it arrives. Motor off while parked: the slot is held mechanically (the follower sits in a cam detent), IHOLD=0.

items.title: 2.6 Homing (the "start up thing")
items.text: Power-up does not home: state 0 at boot, nothing in FUN_080111a0 or main starts it. Homing begins only on F18, F24, or the driver-reset handler (2.8). In the stock host flow the first F18/F24 must be sent by firmwareExe; "who sends it at printer start" is not in this binary, and F18 was not found in STOCK_HOST_RELEASE.md (host side not examined by me). Home sensor: PB9 (GPIOB 0x200), input pull-up, 0 = triggered. 1. State 1: read PB9. Triggered (0): PA6 low, flag 0, count 0, state 2, PB1 low. Not triggered: PA6 high, flag 1, count 0, state 3, PB1 low. (Both: one tick.) 2. State 2 (back off): runs exactly 4096 steps (count > 0xfff) in the negative direction (does NOT stop when the sensor clears). Then count = 0 and re-read PB9: still triggered -> state 0x7e (error); else PA6 high, flag 1, state 3. 3. State 3 (forward seek, DIR high): checked on every STEP-low phase: stop when PB9 == 0 or count > 0x3fff. If count < 0x4000 -> state 4, else state 0x7e. count = 0. 4. State 4: count = 0, 0x200001e8 = 0, PB1 high. If 0x20000098 == 1 -> PB1 high, FFS_state = 0x7f, 0x20000098 = 0 (slot move skipped). Else dispatch on target 0x2000021b: 0 -> 0x0c, 1 -> 7 (and target cleared), 2 -> 0x12, 3 -> 0x1d, 4 -> 0x28; the target is cleared to 0 when 1-4 is consumed (F18 afterwards goes to neutral). Worst case ~ 4096 + 16384 steps = 3.2 s. So F18 at power-up = find slot 1 edge, then move to neutral 2048 counts, state 5. F24 C1 = find the edge, stop there, motor off. A failed homing leaves state 0x7e (126) with 0x20000098 unchanged (if it was set it stays 1, so F112 keeps answering "error"; F15 or a new F18/F24 recover).

items.title: 2.7 F30 manual move
items.text: F30 D sets state 0x80: PB1 low, state 0x81: moves from the current count to n (absolute count, positive up to any int; no limit, no homing), PB1 high on arrival, stays in state 129. Position counter keeps its value.

items.title: 2.8 Autonomous driver-reset handler (FUN_08017ad4)
items.text: Both TMC reply ISRs compare the GCONF reply low byte with 0xdc. A mismatch sets 0x20000260. Next main pass: planner reset + PA5 high + PB1 high (FUN_08015d28), re-write the TMC init to BOTH drivers (FUN_08011bc8), FFS_state = 1 (re-home), 0x20000098 = 1, flag cleared. Result: homing runs and ends in FFS_state 0x7f (127) with the selector parked at home (slot 1, off), until the host does F15/F112. Only triggers when a GCONF read is answered (F13 / F41 / F50 / F60 requests); no periodic polling in the firmware.

items.title: 3.1 Sampling
items.text: Main loop counter reaches 1001 then one blocking ADC conversion per input (FUN_080110dc(adc, channel)) is taken. Every input keeps a counter of 1..20 accumulated samples; on the 21st sample the average (sum/20) is stored and the counter restarts (the 21st sample is discarded). Conversion time and main-pass period were not measured (not found), so the averaging period is "21 x 1001 main passes". Inputs (idx = slot-1): silk idx0 ADC2 ch6 (PC0), idx1 ADC2 ch8 (PC2), idx2 ADC4 ch3 (PB12), idx3 ADC4 ch4 (PB14); speed idx0 ADC2 ch7 (PC1), idx1 ADC2 ch9 (PC3), idx2 ADC3 ch5 (PB13), idx3 ADC4 ch5 (PB15). The connector number to slot assumption is an assumption (to verify).

items.title: 3.2 Silk (filament present) per channel, flags 0x200001bf[i] (reset value 1,1,1,1), averages 0x20000134[i]
items.text:
• avg < 900 or avg > 3100 -> flag = 1. On a 0 -> 1 change the insert bit is set: 0x200001d0 |= 1<<i.
  • 1001 <= avg <= 2999 -> flag = 0 and the insert bit i is cleared.
  • 900..1000 and 3000..3100: hold (hysteresis, no change).
  • F23 C clears bit n-1 only; it re-arms only after the flag has gone 0 and returned to 1 (or it never was set).
  • At boot the flags are 1: a lane already loaded at power-up creates no insert bit; an empty lane clears its flag after the first average.
  • silk_state (F13) and F12 use the same flags, bit i = slot i+1 (F13 only).
  • Nothing in the firmware reads these flags to act (readers: F12, F13, ADC loop only). No auto load, no LED pattern on insert.

items.title: 3.3 Speed (movement) sensors and stall_state
items.text:
• Raw averages 0x20000144[i] (uint16).
  • Flags 0x2000015e[i] and event latch 0x20000162[i] in the ADC loop (thresholds: outside 1397..2636, asserted when < 1200 or > 2800, cleared inside 1397..2636) have no readers: dead code.
  • The live "stall" data comes from SysTick (every 20 ms, per channel idx): index k = 0x2000021c[i] (byte); if k < 50: buf[k] = avg[i] (50-sample ring per channel: 0x2000139c, 0x20001400, 0x20001464, 0x200014c8); d = |buf[k] - buf[0]|; if d >= 15: stall flag 0x200001d9[i] = 1, counter 0x2000152c[i]++ (wraps to 0 above 0xffffffef), k = 0x31 (then k++ -> 0x32, next tick k = 0, i.e. a new window); else (d < 15) and k == 0x31 (50 samples = 1 s with no change >= 15 counts): flag = 0. k++ each tick. When k >= 50: k = 0.
  • So the bit named "stall" is 1 when the speed-sensor ADC average moved by 15 or more counts inside the last window (filament MOVING) and returns to 0 after one quiet second. The counter F40 counts these movement windows. Counter i is cleared when an F10/F11 for channel i starts. (Name/meaning for the host: inferred from the code. How firmwareExe uses it is host side.)
  • F14 = flags, F13 stall_state = bits (bit i = slot i+1), F21 "stall:" = the raw speed averages (not flags), F40 = counters.
  • Stall never stops or changes the motors.

items.title: 3.4 LEDs / PB5, PB6
items.text: PB5 high, PB6 low at boot (FUN_08011b48) and on F15. State 0x7e: PB5 low, PB6 high. No other writers found. Which of D4 (OK) / D5 (ERR) is PB5 / PB6 is not found in the binary (board photo not read); the pattern is consistent with PB5 = OK, PB6 = ERR (inferred).

items.title: 4. Boot, bootloader, F37
items.text:
Reset (Reset_Handler 0x080101ac) -> SystemInit FUN_08012428 (HSE, PLL, 144 MHz, flash wait states, VTOR written) -> __main (RAM init decompress 0x08010f44, 0x490 B to 0x20000000) -> FUN_08015ea0: 1. VTOR = 0x08010000 (FUN_08011ba4). 2. FUN_080111a0: NVIC priority grouping 0x700; USART1 115200 + DMA RX 200 B + IDLE IRQ (FUN_080142b4, FUN_08012d20); ring buffer init FUN_08017b30; ADC init FUN_08011a2c; UART7/USART2 9600 + DMA (FUN_080143e4, FUN_08012be4); TMC init writes on USART2 and UART7 (FUN_08011bc8, values in STOCK_MOTOR_DRIVE.md); PB5 high, PB6 low (FUN_08011b48); 0x20000100 = 0; start TIM5/TIM6/SysTick (FUN_08015e60). 3. FUN_080164a4 (motor outputs off, planner reset), then the main loop. No delays, no homing, no self test, no reply sent at boot. FFS_state = 0.

F37 (0x0801378a): FUN_08011fe0(0x0800D000, 0xFFFFFFFF) = unlock flash, clear status 0x35, erase the page 0x0800D000, program word 0xFFFFFFFF, lock; then FAULTMASK set, DSB, SCB->AIRCR = 0x05FA0004 | (AIRCR & 0x700), loop. No reply. The bootloader (0x08000000-0x0800FFFF) is not in this file; it sees the erased flag word and waits for the upload. Bootloader protocol (XMODEM-like, 115200 8E1, C sync, 1030-byte frames, CRC16 0x1021, ACK 0x06 / NAK 0x15, EOT 0x04, written from 0x08010000, only listens right after power-up or the flag state) is from Kalico firmware on the IFS (not re-derived here). How the bootloader validates the app (SP check etc.) is not found.

items.title: 5. Things the firmware does without host commands
items.text: Everything else in the app is passive: 1. ADC sampling (silk flags, insert bits, speed averages). 2. SysTick movement/stall latch and counters. 3. Driver-reset recovery (2.8), only after a host-initiated GCONF read shows a changed GCONF. 4. State-machine progress in TIM6 (settle states, planner-empty detection, F11 stop). No replies are ever sent unasked, no periodic TMC polling, no watchdog, no timeouts, no auto-load on insert, no stall response, no idle motor release (F10 leaves the feed enabled until F112; F11 end releases both).

items.title: 6. Not found / unverified
items.text:
• Time per main-loop pass and ADC conversion (so sensor averaging period in ms).
  • Which host command first homes the selector at printer start.
  • Bootloader internals beyond F37 and the flashing protocol.
  • Physical meaning of D4/D5 vs PB5/PB6.
  • Planner block splitting limits for very long L (the F10 L1000 used by the host is accepted by the host flow; exact limits not analysed).

items.title: Stock IFS odometer (stall), host E0109 monitor, LEDs
items.text: Sources: the Ghidra decompile of the stock ifs.bin, the decompile of firmwareExe (SerialObject::*, Print::*, Status::*, Config::*) and the IFS initial RAM image. Nothing was run on a printer. "not found" = looked for, absent. "inferred" = from code reading only.

items.title: A1. Sampling (main loop FUN_08015ea0, addresses are decompile lines/functions)
items.text:
• Speed inputs, idx = lane-1: idx0 ADC2 ch7 (PC1, DAT_080162c4=0x40020c00), idx1 ADC2 ch9 (PC3), idx2 ADC3 ch5 (PB13, DAT_080162ec=0x40021800), idx3 ADC4 ch5 (PB15, DAT_080162d8=0x40021c00). Each read is a blocking single conversion FUN_080110dc(adc, ch) (FUN_08010fcc(adc,ch,1,7), sample-time code 7).
  • Gate: main-pass counter uVar5 counts passes; when > 1000 (every 1001st pass) it reads ALL 8 inputs (4 silk + 4 speed) back to back. No gating by selected lane, active lane, feed state or any command: all four lanes are always sampled and always processed.
  • Per input a counter runs 1..20: samples 1..20 are summed; on the 21st sample the stored value = sum / 20 (integer, uint16, raw 12-bit counts 0..4095) and the 21st sample itself is discarded, counter restarts. So the stored average avg[i] (RAM 0x20000144 + 2*i, F21 "stall:" values) is a new value every 21 x 1001 main passes.
  • Time per main pass and ADC conversion time: not found (no measurement, no cycle count done). So the update period of avg in ms is unknown; SysTick below samples it every 20 ms regardless, so consecutive SysTick samples are often identical.
  • Dead code (no readers): per-lane flags at 0x2000015e/0x20000162 (outside 1397..2636 / <1200 / >2800 tests).

items.title: A2. Movement latch (SysTick 50 Hz = 20 ms, vec_15 0x080121b2 -> FUN_080121bc)
items.text:
SysTick reload = SystemCoreClock/50 - 1 (FUN_08015834); SystemCoreClock = 144000000 (initial RAM 0x20000488 = 0x08954400), so exactly 20 ms. Per lane i (independent, same code x4), state k = byte 0x2000021c[i], ring buf = uint16[50] (0x2000139c, 0x20001400, 0x20001464, 0x200014c8), flag = byte 0x200001d9[i], counter = uint32 0x2000152c[i]:

tick(i):
  if k < 50:                      # 0x32
      buf[k] = avg[i]
      d = abs(buf[k] - buf[0])    # compared against the FIRST sample of the window
      if d >= 15:                 # exact: d < 0xf is "quiet"
          flag = 1
          cnt += 1                # if cnt > 0xffffffef after increment -> cnt = 0
          k = 0x31
      elif k == 0x31:             # 49: whole window quiet
          flag = 0
      k += 1
  else:                           # k >= 50
      k = 0                       # this tick takes no sample
- Window: baseline buf[0] = avg at k=0; compared every 20 ms against baseline for k=1..49. - Movement seen (d >= 15 counts): flag = 1, counter + 1, window ends at once: k = 0x31 then +1 = 0x32, next tick resets k = 0 (no sample), the tick after takes the new baseline. Gap between counter increments is therefore >= 3 ticks (60 ms), at most one increment per window. - Quiet window: flag cleared at the tick where k == 49, i.e. 50 samples after the baseline = 1.00 s; then one extra reset tick, so full quiet cycle = 51 ticks = 1.02 s. "One quiet second" is right: flag = 1 stays until a full window passes with every sample within < 15 counts of its baseline. - Flag meaning: 1 = filament MOVING (naming "stall" is misleading). Counter = number of movement windows. - Not gated by lane selection, motor state or any command. - Counter clear: only the feed state machine (FUN_0801900c cases for F10 start: counter[0] in states 10 and 0xe; counters [1] and [2] in the following state pairs; counters [2]/[3] also via DAT_08019bf8+8/+0xc; exact state-to-command mapping per lane not re-derived). Flags are never cleared except by the quiet window. Not cleared by F14/F40 reads. RAM init = 0.

items.title: A3. Reply fields
items.text:
• F13: F13 ok. FFS_state: %d silk_state: %d chan: %d ffs_channels_insert: %d stall_state: %d jinsi_GCONF: ... qiehuan_GCONF: ... . stall_state = byte 0x200000da = f[3]<<3 | f[2]<<2 | f[1]<<1 | f[0] from the flags 0x200001d9[0..3] (bit i = lane i+1; 1 = moving). silk_state = same from silk flags 0x200001bf (1 = filament present at the lane sensor).
  • F14: F14 ok. stall: a b c d raw flags 0/1.
  • F40: F40 ok.stall count: C1: %d C2: %d C3: %d C4: %d uint32 counters.
  • F21: raw avg arrays (silk first, then speed).
  • Stall never changes motor behaviour in the firmware.

items.title: B1. Feed of data: SerialObject::recvQueryFourInOneSt 005fa660 (thread)
items.text:
• Loop. If this+0x2f0 (setFourInOneBusy: set during load/unload/cut/feed waits) is set: sleep(1), no F13 sent.
  • Else send F13 via sendCmdToUart4. No "ok" in reply: fail counter++; after >= 4 consecutive failures (and having been online before) sigIfsStatus(false); sleep(1) between failures.
  • Reply tokenised with regex [: ], empty tokens skipped: tok5 = silk_state (-> iVar5), tok9 = ffs_channels_insert (-> iVar8, used for auto-load), tok11 = stall_state. (tok3 FFS_state, tok13 GCONF are used by Status::slotSendCmdF13Recv 007c49b4, which only displays the bits in Status::updateIfsOdometerStatus 007c46b4 as per-lane OK/not-OK labels.)
  • Only when MainWindow::getMainMachineStatus() == 5 (print running; set 5 in Print::delayStartPrint 0068c4c8 and Print::homePrintResumeFinish 006822e4; 0 idle, 2/3 pause, 6 resume click, 9 cancel) it calls sigIFSMottorNoRunning(stall_state, 0, silk_state). The second argument ("vibr") is the constant 0 (never filled).
  • Polling period: status 5 (printing) -> sleep(1) per loop = one F13 about every 1 s plus the reply time (the IFS also spends ~8 ms in F13 reading both TMCs); status 0 (idle) -> usleep(200000) (200 ms); any other status -> sleep(1).
  • F14 and F40 are NEVER sent by the host (no string "F14"/"F40" in SerialObject). The only odometer input is the F13 stall_state bit mask. F40 counters are not used host-side.

items.title: B2. SerialObject::slotIFSMottorNoRunning 005f369c (slot of sigIFSMottorNoRunning, signal index 0x2b; only emitter is recvQueryFourInOneSt 005fac50)
items.text: Args: p1 = stall_state mask, p2 = 0, p3 = silk_state mask. Outer gate, all must hold: 1. this+0x2e4 != 0: copy of startPrintPthread param 6 (Print+0x9a, a per-job flag from the Print dialog ctor param 7; exact meaning not resolved, inferred "this print uses IFS/multicolour"). 2. this+0x2e2 != 0: IFS online (slotIfsStatus 005f3bc0 sets it from the F13 poll result). 3. this+0x98 != 0: this is Config::getMileageEnable() read in the SerialObject ctor (005e5608). Config key OdometerEnable (JSON, default false, written by MoreInfo::on_btnMileage_clicked 005a49d8). Setting is read at construct time; the only other setter is setIroning 005defe8 (identical-code-folded name) called from MachineInfo::on_btnPower_clicked. So the E0109 monitor is OFF unless OdometerEnable is true. 4. this+0x2e0 == 0 (m_refulling: toolchange pending/in progress). 5. this+0xd0 != 0 (IFS filament loaded/active: 1 after changeChannel with param_2 == 0 and after a successful pause-resume; 0 at initPrint and at timeOutPause). Then: ch = *(this + (m_channel(+0x248) + 0x94)*4) = 1-based lane from the tool->lane map at this+0x250 (16 ints, default (i&3)+1); u = ch - 1. m_channel (+0x248) comes from Klipper virtual_sdcard.channel in doQueryResponse. Inner gate: (silk_state >> u) & 1 (filament present in that lane) AND E = this+0xc0 > 0 AND E != this+0xc4 (last evaluated E). - this+0xc0 = gcode_move.gcode_position[3] (E position in mm, absolute) from the objects/query reply; updated in doQueryResponse only when not refuelling (+0x2e1==0) and not paused (+0x8a==0) and the position changed. initPrint and ctor zero +0xc0/+0xc4; serialPrint sends G92 E0 at print start. Action when the inner gate passes: +0xc4 = E (so each new E value is evaluated once), then - if (stall_state >> u) & 1 == 0 (lane NOT moving): m_stallCount[ch] (int at this + ch*4 + 0x29c) += 1; if the new value > 200 (i.e. 201st evaluation): E0109 fires. - else (lane moving): m_stallCount[ch] = 0. Counters (16 ints at this+0x2a0..0x2df) are zeroed at the start of serialPrint 006042e4 (after sleep(2)). Time estimate: a poll evaluates only when E changed since the previous evaluation. During normal extrusion that is every poll (~1 s), so about 201 s of continuous "E advanced but lane not moving" polls; any poll with the lane flag = 1 resets the count to 0.

items.title: B3. What fires
items.text: After count > 200: debug "IFS odometer roller: ", then readM25() (signal index 0x1b, connected in Print::Print to Print::on_pause_clicked: the print is PAUSED through the normal UI pause path), then sigIFSError("E0109: " + tr(...) + number(ch) , wiki URL or empty (URL "https://wiki.flashforge.com/en/ad5x/error_code_list_ad5x#e0109-ifs-odometer-roller-1234-not-moving" whenthis+0x1f5!= 0), "E0109"). Print::slotIFSError 006796b8 shows the ErrorDialog and MainWindow::setErrorCode("E0109"). The counter for that lane is reset to 0 afterwards. No F-commands are sent, motors are not touched by this path. Message text pieces come from tr() calls whose strings were not resolved (wiki text: "IFS odometer roller 1/2/3/4 not moving").

items.title: C. LEDs (IFS firmware)
items.text: Pins: GPIOB 0x40010c00. Boot init FUN_08011b48: PB5 and PB6 configured output push-pull (config word 0x10030020 / 0x10030040), then FUN_08011984(GPIOB,0x20) (write +0x10 = set high) and FUN_08011980(GPIOB,0x40) (write +0x14 = clear low). Complete list of writers (all code searched: every literal-pool reference to 0x40010c00 and the F-command region): | Event | PB5 (0x20) | PB6 (0x40) | where | |---|---|---|---| | Boot | high | low | FUN_08011b48 from FUN_080111a0 | | F15 | high | low | F15 body 0x080134d6 (also FFS_state = 5, reply "F15 ok. ") | | FFS_state 126 (0x7e), homing failure | low | high | FUN_0801900c case 0x7e (also PB1 high); runs on every TIM6 tick (78 us) while the state stays 126 | | FFS_state 127 (0x7f), all other states, all other commands | unchanged | unchanged | no LED writes | State 126 is entered only from homing: state 2 (back-off done and PB9 reads 0) or state 3 (seek count >= 0x4000). The ERR pattern stays until F15 or a reset; a later successful homing (F18/F24/driver-reset recovery) does NOT restore it. No blink, no timing, no insert/stall/command indication anywhere. Which pin is D4 (OK) vs D5 (ERR) and the electrical polarity: not found in the binary or in board/ifs1.jpg (back side, LEDs not visible; no schematic). Pattern consistent with PB5 = OK, PB6 = ERR (inferred, polarity unknown).

items.title: Python model (exact numbers)
items.text:
TICK=0.020; THRESH=15; WIN=50
class Lane:
    k=0; buf=[0]*50; moving=False; count=0
    def tick(self, avg):
        if self.k < WIN:
            self.buf[self.k]=avg
            if abs(avg-self.buf[0]) >= THRESH:
                self.moving=True; self.count=(self.count+1)&0xffffffff
                self.k=0x31
            elif self.k==0x31: self.moving=False
            self.k+=1
        else: self.k=0
# avg: sum of 20 ADC samples //20, refreshed every 21 sample rounds (period not measured)
# stall_state = sum(l.moving<<i); host poll F13 ~1 s while printing
# host: if gate and silk_bit and E>0 and E!=lastE: lastE=E; cnt = cnt+1 if not moving else 0; if cnt>200: pause + E0109, cnt=0

items.title: IFS in AFC
items.text: The IFS runs as a unit of AFC (Automated Filament Changer). AFC is only the framework: AFC_IFS.py makes the IFS behave like the stock firmware. The options, flows and commands are in config-docs/IFS.md in AD5X-FS. This page records how the unit is set up and why.

items.title: Where AFC lives
items.text:
AFC is not installed separately. Only the parts the IFS uses ship, in our own repos:

  • kalico-ad5x, klippy/extras/: the 16 AFC modules Klippy loads with this config, from AFC commit 5ea84ea with a source line added to each header (full hash 5ea84ea6fab75b9b49db090f309154d1e52272bb): AFC, AFC_utils, AFC_logger, AFC_respond, AFC_functions, AFC_error, AFC_stats, AFC_assist, AFC_prep, AFC_spool, AFC_lane, AFC_stepper, AFC_extruder, AFC_unit, AFC_BoxTurtle, AFC_HTLF. Next to them AFC_IFS.py and ad5x_filament_sensor.py. The other AFC units and features (hubs, buffers, LEDs, tip forming, toolchanger, OpenAMS) are left out; a config that adds one of those sections would need its module added.
  • AD5X-FS, fs/usr/data/config/AFC/: AFC.cfg, AFC_Macro_Vars.cfg (only _AFC_CUT_TIP_VARS), AFC_Hardware-IFS.cfg and ifs_macros.cfg. No AFC macro files are used: AFC_IFS replaces AFC's park, poop, brush and cut with ADX_PARK, ADX_POOP, ADX_BRUSH and ADX_CUT, which do the stock moves (ADX_POOP does the stock chute flush, also when no IFS lane is loaded); ADX_CUT reads _AFC_CUT_TIP_VARS.
  • [include AFC/*.cfg] goes in printer.cfg above the SAVE_CONFIG block.
  • VarFile in AFC.cfg is /usr/data/openad5x/klipper/config/AFC/AFC.var. 10-klipper.sh creates AFC.var.unit and AFC.var (empty, {}) before Klipper starts, because AFC stops with an error while they are missing; AFC fills them in.

Things to know:

  • No extra Python packages are needed: AFC imports only the standard library and Klippy modules.
  • Kalico's ADC API is setup_adc_sample(sample_time, sample_count), not setup_minmax.
  • A change to a Python module needs a full Klippy process restart. RESTART and printer/restart keep the old module.
  • [AFC_extruder extruder] has no pin_tool_start, because the toolhead filament sensor is analog (eboard PA3). The sensor is declared with u1_filament_sensor_name: fill_sensor.
  • The unit section has no hub: a unit hub must name an [AFC_hub]. The lanes and both AFC_stepper sections use hub: direct.
  • Lanes without a load pin start with load_state True. AFC_IFS applies the first silk reading so lanes show their real state.
  • AFC's lane move speeds are set to the stock feed speed (20 mm/s). The AFC defaults were 50 and 150 mm/s.
  • Command and macro names must be letters and underscores only. Klipper's parser reads the command as the first letter run plus the digits after it, so a command called AD5X_CUT is read as AD5 and never dispatches. That is why the commands are named ADX_....

items.title: Motors
items.text:
Feed Selector Step PA0 PA7 Direction PA1 (positive = into the IFS toward the printer) PA6 (positive = home seek, count up) Enable PA5, active low PB1, active low TMC UART PA3 / PA2 PC5 / PC4 Microsteps 8 8 Distance rotation_distance: 4.655 (343.696 steps/mm) rotation_distance: 360, 2048 full steps per turn
  • The first version of the pin table used swapped helper names, so every output polarity was wrong and neither motor was ever enabled. The table above comes from the stock motor table.
  • SET_STEPPER_ENABLE followed by DUMP_TMC REGISTER=IOIN is not a reliable check of the enable polarity here, because the reads lag the enable.
  • The stock firmware runs the drivers in spreadCycle. In Kalico stealthchop_threshold: 0 means stealthChop at all speeds (any value sets en_pwm_mode), so there is no stealthchop_threshold line. In stealthChop the feed driver showed ola=1 olb=1 and the motor did not turn.
  • Steps are single-edge (step_pulse_duration: 0.000002), as in stock (CHOPCONF dedge=0).

items.title: Driver current
items.text: The clone drivers deliver far less current than spec in vsense=1. Kalico encodes 0.138 A as vsense=1, CS 17, and with that the selector clicked over every cam lobe and the feed skipped steps at 20 mm/s. The stock registers (vsense=0, IRUN 9, the same nominal current) run cleanly. Kalico's TMC2209 helper never drops to vsense=0, so kalico-ad5x's tmc2209.py accepts raw driver_<NAME> fields, and the config sets the stock registers directly: driver_VSENSE: 0, driver_IRUN: 9, driver_IHOLD: 0, driver_SHAFT: 1, driver_INDEX_OTPW: 1 and driver_TPWMTHRS: 0, besides the chopper settings. See the table in Stock IFS firmware.

items.title: The feed motor and the extruder
items.text:
AFC enables the lane's drive motor and syncs it to the extruder when it activates an extruder, and during prep, load and unload. With the IFS drive at stock IRUN 9 and IHOLD 0 (coils shorted at standstill), that held the clamped lane back and the extruder slipped: the first Benchy printed nothing. With the drive disabled, E30 and E100 came out fine.

Stock keeps the feed motor off while printing, with the extruder pulling through the clamped lane. So the drive stepper's sync_to_extruder in AFC_IFS releases the motor instead of syncing it. Feed moves (lane.move) still enable the motor as normal. Where stock pushes the lane in step with the extruder (the flush), the unit syncs it explicitly for that move only.

items.title: Lane lengths
items.text:
• From the inlet stop (filament pushed in until the feed gear) to the toolhead sensor trip is about 640 mm. Measured on lane 1 and lane 2; the stock first-load limit is 650 mm.
  • From the point where a hand-pulled tip rests, 188 mm to the toolhead sensor trip was measured with FORCE_MOVE.
  • A parked lane sits 70 mm back (dist_hub: 70 per lane, the stock UnloadIFSSpace).
  • tool_stn (sensor to nozzle) is measured at 50 mm: with the nozzle at 220 °C and the lane and extruder pushed together, filament came out between 45 and 55 mm past the toolhead sensor. Stock has no tool_stn: after the sensor trip it stops the IFS and flushes with G1 E90 while the IFS pushes, so it purges 90 mm from the sensor.
  • CALIBRATE_AFC BOWDEN= does not work as is: for direct lanes it first retracts until the load (silk) sensor clears, and that sensor is at the lane inlet before the feed gear.

items.title: Purge chute
items.text:
Stock enters and leaves the chute along Y only. AFC's Park, Poop and Brush macros move diagonally in one G1 X.. Y.. (there is no approach option) and can catch the chute walls. AFC_IFS provides ADX_PARK, ADX_POOP and ADX_BRUSH, and at connect it sets AFC's park_cmd, poop_cmd and wipe_cmd to them, but only where AFC.cfg still has the AFC defaults. AFC.cfg is trimmed to the settings the IFS uses.

AFC's order is: unload = cut, park; load = poop, wipe (kick off), wipe. direct_load in AFC loads to the nozzle on insert, where stock parks. HTLF assumes home means no lane pressed, while the IFS home is slot 1.

items.title: Unload
items.text:
Unload follows stock (see Stock load and unload): the lane retracts until the toolhead sensor clears, and the extruder never retries. AFC does the opposite (extruder retries up to tool_max_unload_attempts, then a blind lane retract), so tool_max_unload_attempts is 0 and the unit replaces the retract.

The reason is that the toolhead sensor sits on the lane side of the cutter, so only the IFS retracting the lane clears it. Pulling the filament out by hand moves the sensor from 0.007 to 0.317.

items.title: Selector
items.text:
• The unit homes once per startup, tracks the selector position and moves from slot to slot, as stock does (AFC_HTLF would re-home after every lane). It re-homes after a homing failure and when a different lane is selected.
  • After a move the selector parks at the neutral position (45°), because otherwise lane 1 stays clamped.
  • QUERY_ENDSTOPS shows IFS_1_home:TRIGGERED at home, and AFC_HOME_UNIT UNIT=IFS_1 works.
  • The speed is the stock 70.43°/s with no ramp (selector_movement_speed: 70.43, selector_movement_accel: 0).

items.title: Open
items.text: • AFC_Macro_Vars.cfg only holds the cut position (_AFC_CUT_TIP_VARS, read by ADX_CUT); park, purge and brush are the stock moves in ADX_PARK, ADX_POOP and ADX_BRUSH.

items.title: Board
items.text:
FFP0302_Main_Board_V1.0.4 (2024-08-05), FlashForge part 20004780001.

  • U5: Nations N32G455, with an X1 12.000 MHz crystal
  • U3 and U4: stepper drivers. The marking reads MS35776, a TMC2209-compatible UART clone
  • U1: GM3085E RS485 transceiver
  • J1 "485-IN": 4-pin Microfit with 24 V, GND, A, B
  • J2 to J5, Silk1 to Silk4: GND, VCC, Speed, Silk (per slot: filament present, and movement)
  • Zero_CHK: SIG, VCC, GND. The selector home sensor, on PB9
  • J8 "A" and J7 "B": motor connectors, with R500 sense resistors
  • J9: VCC, CLK, DIO, GND. This is SWD, the recovery path with an ST-Link
  • J6: 3-pin, on the back, unlabelled
  • D4 (OK) and D5 (ERR) LEDs

items.title: Chip: Nations N32G455
items.text:
• The ADC init uses 0x40020C00, 0x40021800 and 0x40021C00, which are exactly the N32G45x ADC2, ADC3 and ADC4. ADC3 and ADC4 exist on the G455 only.
  • The UART at 0x40015400 (PC4 and PC5, 9600) is a timer on the STM32F1 and GD32F30x, and UART7 on the N32G45x.
  • Clock: CFGR |= 0x30000 | 0x081C0000 is HSE/2 x24 (PLLMUL bit 4 at bit 27). The 12 MHz crystal gives 144 MHz, the N32G45x maximum (the GD32F303 maximum is 120).
  • The ADC on PB12 to PB15 is on ADC3 and ADC4, which means the N32G455.
  • The hardware FPU is used (vldr and vmov d0): Cortex-M4F.
  • Kalico supports it as MACH_N32G455. It reports itself as stm32f103xe, uses STM32_FLASH_START_10000 (a 64 KiB bootloader offset), and the default RAM_SIZE for the N32G45x is 0x10000.
  • The AD5X mainboards also report stm32f103xe at 144 MHz, so they are probably N32G45x too.

items.title: Pins
items.text:
Pin Mode Use PA9 / PA10 AF_PP / IPU USART1 TX/RX, 115200: host link (ttyS4) PA11 Out_PP, low at init RS485 direction for USART1: high = transmit, low = receive PA2 / PA3 AF_PP / IPU USART2 TX/RX, 9600, DMA1: the feed motor's TMC ("jinsi") PC4 / PC5 AF_PP / IPU UART7 TX/RX, 9600, DMA2: the selector motor's TMC ("qiehuan") PA0 Out_PP feed motor STEP PA1 Out_PP feed motor DIR, with a per-motor invert flag PA5 Out_PP feed motor EN, active low: high at init and in the F112 stop, low to enable PA7 Out_PP selector motor STEP, toggled per timer tick PA6 Out_PP selector motor DIR: high = positive (count up) and home seek, low = back off PB1 Out_PP selector motor EN, active low: low while moving, high at init, on arrival and in the F112 stop PB9 IPU selector home sensor, 0 = triggered PB5 (high), PB6 (low) Out_PP LEDs (probably D4 and D5), only set at init PC0 / PC2 / PB12 / PB14 analog Silk1 to Silk4 filament sensors (ADC2 ch6, ADC2 ch8, ADC4 ch3, ADC4 ch4) PC1 / PC3 / PB13 / PB15 analog Speed1 to Speed4 movement sensors (ADC2 ch7, ADC2 ch9, ADC3 ch5, ADC4 ch5)

Peripherals the stock firmware uses: GPIOA, GPIOB, GPIOC, AFIO, EXTI, USART1 to USART3, TIM1 to TIM8 and 0x40015000/0x40015400, DMA1, RCC, FLASH and PWR.

items.title: Sensors
items.text:
• Each input is averaged over 20 samples.
  • Silk (filament present): the flag is set when the average is below 900 or above 3100, and cleared when it is between 1001 and 2999. A rising edge sets a bit in ffs_channels_insert.
  • Speed (movement): the window is 1400 to 2636 or 1200 to 2800, and the values are logged to ring buffers that feed stall_state.
  • The slot order (bit 0 to 3 = slot 1 to 4) is assumed to match the Silk1 to Silk4 connector numbering.

items.title: Open questions
items.text:
• What PB5 and PB6 do (probably the OK and ERR LEDs D4 and D5)
  • Which motor connector (J8 "A" or J7 "B") is the feed motor and which is the selector
  • The driver chip marking (MS35776?) and how closely it matches the TMC2209 in Kalico
  • Whether the R500 resistors are the sense resistors

items.title: Kalico firmware on the IFS
items.text: The IFS runs Kalico (kalico-ad5x) in place of the stock firmware, as its own Klipper MCU: [mcu ifs] with serial: /dev/ttyS4, baud: 115200 and restart_method: command. FlashForge's bootloader is kept, and Kalico is flashed at 0x08010000 with the stock IFSCommand.

items.title: Build
items.text:
The Kalico build config for the IFS is mcu-firmware/ad5x/config/kalico-ifs.config in AD5X-FS:

  • MACH_N32G455, CLOCK_FREQ 144000000, CLOCK_REF_FREQ 12000000
  • FLASH_APPLICATION_ADDRESS 0x8010000
  • STM32_SERIAL_USART1, SERIAL_BAUD 115200
  • STM32_FLASHFORGE_IFS=y, which selects the IFS-specific behaviour below

The data dictionary reports stm32f103xe, 144 MHz and 115200, with RESERVE_PINS_serial PA10,PA9 and RESERVE_PINS_rs485 PA11. The Intel hex layout matches the stock ifs.hex.

items.title: Stack pointer
items.text: Stock uses an initial SP of 0x20007498. The eboard bootloader refuses an app with SP 0x20010000 and accepts 0x20020000. For the IFS, kalico-ad5x sets RAM_SIZE 0x8000 when STM32_FLASHFORGE_IFS is on, which gives SP 0x20008000, and the IFS bootloader accepts it. The mainboard and eboard builds are unchanged.

items.title: Clock
items.text: The stock clock is HSE/2 x24, which is 144 MHz from the 12 MHz crystal. kalico-ad5x's original N32G45x support was fixed at 128 MHz and its generic STM32F1 clock_setup() gave only 120 MHz with that crystal, so kalico-ad5x carries a 144 MHz clock patch. See Clock. The IFS build also drops to HSI and stops the PLL first, like the stock SystemInit.

items.title: Bootloader request
items.text:
The stock firmware reached its bootloader with the F37 command (see Stock IFS firmware). Kalico has a board patch that does the same: on a bootloader request it erases page 0x0800D000 and resets, so reflashing over ttyS4 keeps working.

To request the bootloader from a running Kalico IFS, write ~ \x1c Request Serial Bootloader!! ~ at 115200 8N1 to ttyS4 (Klipper must not be holding the port), then run the catch script straight away.

items.title: Flashing
items.text:
The stock IFSCommand protocol is XMODEM-like, 115200 8E1:

  • The host sends C until the bootloader answers 0x06 (or 0x07).
  • Frames are 0x01, a sequence byte, a 16-bit little-endian length, 1024 bytes of data (padded with 0xFF) and a CRC16-CCITT (polynomial 0x1021, initial value 0), which is 1030 bytes. Each frame is acknowledged with 0x06 or rejected with 0x15. Then EOT 0x04 is answered with 0x06.
  • There are no addresses: the data is written from 0x08010000.
  • IFSCommand flushes after every write and waits 5 s per read. Its stm32Reboot and stm32UpdateFLag GPIO functions are never called.

The tools are in AD5X-FS, under fs/usr/data/openad5x/mcu-flash/:

Tool What it does ifs_capture.py <IFSCommand> <hex> <out.frames> Runs IFSCommand against a fake bootloader on a pty and saves its exact frames ifs_catch.py <port> <frames> <seconds> Sends C every 20 ms until the bootloader answers, then the frames and EOT. Works in the power-up window (unplug and replug the IFS cable) or after a bootloader request ad5x-mcu-flash <folder> The installer's flash tool. Flashes the mainboard, the IFS and (staged for the next power cycle) the eboard from a folder of mcu-firmware/ad5x images. See Flashing

The bootloader only listens for a short window right after the IFS powers up (while the flag at 0x0800D000 is set).

ad5x-mcu-flash picks the way by asking Moonraker whether Klippy has an mcu ifs. A Kalico IFS gets the request string above. An IFS that still runs FlashForge's firmware gets what FlashForge's control run.sh does: ifsF37 /dev/ttyS4, then IFSCommand ifs.hex /dev/ttyS4.

The way back to the stock firmware is IFSCommand /usr/prog/PROGRAM/control/1.1.1/ifs.hex /dev/ttyS4 while the bootloader is waiting. ifsF37 no longer works once Kalico runs, because Kalico does not know F37.

items.title: The host link
items.text:
The host link is RS485: the AD5X has an RS485 converter on ttyS4, the IFS has a transceiver, and the cable is a 4-pin Microfit 3.0. PA11 is the direction pin, and stock drives it high to transmit and low to receive.

Kalico's src/stm32 has no RS485 control, so the IFS build adds it in serial.c. Two problems had to be solved.

items.title: Direction and turnaround
items.text: The host switches its RS485 driver in hardware (there is no kernel RS485 on ttyS4) and holds the bus briefly after its last byte, while Kalico answers within microseconds. Replies then arrive with the first one or two bytes corrupted. The IFS now waits a short turnaround after the last received byte before driving PA11 high, and the direction change and the TX interrupt are set up with interrupts off.

items.title: Half duplex
items.text:
Klipper pipelines frames, so the host transmits while the IFS answers and both are lost. With AFC, configuring the IFS hung forever, with 956 of 975 bytes retransmitted. The fix is to treat the IFS the way stock does, with the host as master:

  • IFS (serial.c): output waits on a timer and only starts 1 to 2 ms (RS485_GAP_US, RS485_WINDOW_US) after the last received byte. A running burst continues, and the shutdown handler re-arms the timer.
  • Host (klippy/chelper/serialqueue.c): a half-duplex mode, switched on by serialhdl.py when the MCU reports SERIAL_HALF_DUPLEX=1. One block is in flight, and nothing is sent or retransmitted until 2 ms (HALF_DUPLEX_GAP) after the last received byte and 4 ms (HALF_DUPLEX_TX_HOLD) after the host's own transmit ends. When idle, the host writes a lone 0x7e (the MCU ignores leading sync bytes without a NAK), so the IFS gets a turn about every 4 to 5 ms.

After this, configuring the IFS takes 17 ms with no retransmits, the IFS mcu_awake fell from 12.7% to 1.7%, and homing no longer times out.

items.title: Several Klippy instances
items.text: Several Klippy instances fighting over the ports leave the IFS in shutdown (oids already allocated). Busybox ps cuts the command line, so a restart has to match /proc/<pid>/cmdline: stop every klippy.py, then start one. startup/commands/restart-klipper.sh and the 10-klipper.sh loop do this now.

items.title: Known problem
items.text: The IFS link still shows invalid and retransmitted bytes that keep climbing, even at idle. See Status and roadmap.

items.title: Stock IFS firmware
items.text: What the stock IFS firmware (version 3.0.7) does, decoded with Ghidra 12.2 in headless mode.

items.title: Input
items.text:
• ifs.bin from the control package (main-update/control-extracted/ifs.bin), 41168 bytes, sha256 378af71ac647e5865f70e096193acdb19642860a3408457e3b2a44cf01e1c01f
  • The F19 reply is four color. version: 3.0.7
  • ifs.hex in the older factory package (factory-full/usr/prog/PROGRAM/control/1.0.6/) is a different, older build
  • Loaded raw: -loader BinaryLoader -loader-baseAddr 0x08010000 -processor ARM:LE:32:Cortex. The decompile has 243 functions.

items.title: Memory layout
items.text:
• The app is at 0x08010000, size 0xA0D0
  • The bootloader is at 0x08000000 to 0x0800FFFF and is not in the file
  • Initial SP 0x20007498, so at least 30 KB of RAM
  • The flag page is 0x0800D000, inside the bootloader area

items.title: Bootloader entry: F37
items.text:
The command parser (FUN_08012de8) parses F<n> and jumps through a table, with index n - 10. F37 does two things:

  1. Unlocks the flash, clears the status, erases page 0x0800D000, programs the word 0xFFFFFFFF and locks it.
  2. Sets FAULTMASK and writes SCB->AIRCR = 0x05FA0004 | (AIRCR & 0x700) (a system reset).

The app thus wipes its "app valid" flag and resets, and the bootloader then waits for IFSCommand. The stock run.sh does ifsF37 /dev/ttyS4 and then IFSCommand ifs.hex /dev/ttyS4. Any replacement firmware has to do F37 the same way, or reflashing over ttyS4 is lost (only SWD would remain).

items.title: Host protocol (ttyS4, 115200 8N1, text)
items.text:
• A command plus \r\n, then wait about 0.2 s, send 0xFF, and read one reply line. The IFS never talks unasked: every reply comes from the F-command parser.
  • F13 status: FFS_state: %d silk_state: %d chan: %d ffs_channels_insert: %d stall_state: %d jinsi_GCONF: ... qiehuan_GCONF: .... It first reads GCONF from both TMCs. FFS_state is the selector state machine (5 = ready), silk_state has one bit per lane, and stall_state comes from the speed sensors.
  • Motion: F10 feed, F11 exit (unload), F23 and F24 select the channel, F39 release, F112 stop both motors (PA5 and PB1 high).
  • Other: F12 sensors, F14 and F40 stall, F19 version, F22 insert, F30. F41 to F64 read TMC registers (GCONF, GSTAT, DRV_STATUS, CHOPCONF, PWMCONF). F42 S<1|2> I<0-31> sets IRUN live on driver 1 or 2.
  • F10 and F11 take L (length in mm), S (speed in mm/min) and C (channel). The IFS only moves L at S and stops, and the host decides everything else.

items.title: Selector
items.text:
• Bit-banged: one step is STEP high then low. The count goes up or down by one per step.
  • Forward (count up) is DIR high, with GCONF shaft=1.
  • EN is low while moving and high on arrival. The motor is off when parked (IHOLD is 0 too), and held by the mechanism.
  • Speed: a timer interrupt (1 MHz divided by 156, 6410 Hz) toggles STEP, so 3205 microsteps per second, which is a constant 70.43°/s. There is no ramp anywhere.
  • Homing:
    1. If the home sensor is already triggered, back off (DIR low) for up to 4096 steps until it clears. Error 0x7e if it does not.
    2. Go forward for up to 16384 steps until the sensor triggers. Error 0x7e if it is not found.
    3. The count is 0 at the sensor.
  • Positions, in steps from home at 8 microsteps:
Target Position Meaning 1 0 slot 1 (at the home sensor) - 2048 neutral 2 4096 slot 2 - 6144 neutral 3 8192 slot 3 - 10240 neutral 4 12288 slot 4 - 14336 neutral

16384 steps is one full turn, so slots are every 90° and the neutral positions are halfway (45°) between them. 16384 microsteps at 8 microsteps is 2048 full steps per turn (geared).

items.title: Feed motor
items.text:
• The motion code is a generic 5-axis planner (five motors, all five table entries on PA0, PA1 and PA5), with one feed stepper wired. A 2 kHz planner tick calls the step routine N times per tick.
  • Steps per mm come from a value in RAM (343696245 / 1e6): 343.696 steps/mm at 8 microsteps.
  • Stock keeps the feed motor off (EN high) while printing. The extruder pulls the filament through the clamped lane.

items.title: TMC driver setup
items.text:
The same for both drivers. Each driver has its own UART, with separate TX and RX pins, at 9600 baud. Writes are TMC2209 datagrams: sync 0x05, slave address 0, reg | 0x80, 4 bytes, CRC8.

Register Value Decoded GCONF 0x00 0x1dc en_spreadcycle=1, shaft=1, index_otpw=1, pdn_disable=1, mstep_reg_select=1, multistep_filt=1, I_scale_analog=0 IHOLD_IRUN 0x10 0xa0900 IHOLD=0, IRUN=9, IHOLDDELAY=10 TPOWERDOWN 0x11 0x80 128 CHOPCONF 0x6c 0x150082c3 TOFF=3, HSTRT=4, HEND=5, TBL=1, vsense=0, MRES=5 (8 microsteps), intpol=1 PWMCONF 0x70 0xc80d174b stealthChop settings, unused because spreadCycle is on

With the R500 (0.5 ohm) sense resistors, IRUN=9 would be about 0.14 A rms if the chip matches a TMC2209.

items.title: Stock load and unload
items.text:
• Load: F10 C<chn> L650 S1200 until the toolhead sensor (first-load limit 650 mm, 20 mm/s). Tool changes use L1000.
  • Unload (cutFilament): fourInOneCut, G92 E0, then F11 C<lane> L60 S<n> is sent to the IFS first and G1 E-60 F<n> straight after, so they overlap. <n> is 600 mm/min for PLA and ordinary types, 200 or 300 for two special types, and SILK.
  • checkFourInOneUnLoad then polls the IFS with F13 every 200 ms. When it is idle, the host re-clamps the lane (F24) and sends F11 C<lane> L70 S600, and while the toolhead sensor still reads filament it sends the same again, until the IFS reports done or "Unload timeOut!". It never retries with the extruder.
  • UnloadESpace (60), UnloadIFSSpace (70) and UnloadSpeed (600) in Adventurer5M.json are only read by the config initialisation and the delay estimators, not used as command lengths.
  • The total lane retract is 60 + 70 (+70 per retry) at 10 mm/s.
  • The four tubes stay separate up to the 4-in-1 at the toolhead, so a parked lane sits about 70 mm back.

items.title: Stock purge chute moves
items.text:
Stock enters and leaves the chute along Y only. printClearGoPos and clear_go_pos are G1 X52.5, G1 Y220 F12000, G1 Y229 or Y230.5 (F3000 in clear_go_pos). clear_brush is G1 Y220 F3000, G1 X78 F12000, G1 Y230.5, then X65, X73, X65, X73, X65, then G1 X78 and G1 Y220.

More decoded flows are on the other IFS pages: stock host flows, IFS side and load wizard.

items.title: MCU development
items.text:
Goal: run Kalico on the host and on both MCUs, so the IFS can join as a Kalico MCU (see IFS). A Klipper/Kalico host only talks to MCUs built from the same code, so host, mainboard, eboard and IFS switch together.

items.title: Eboard power pins
items.text:
Under Kalico the hotend heater did not heat: with power 1.0 the temperature stayed at 24 °C, and verify_heater shut down with "Heater extruder not heating at expected rate".

  • The stock eboard firmware sets PB1 and PB7 as push-pull outputs in its init, before the main loop, and drives both high. PB1 stays high. PB7 is cleared later in the main loop, once a flag is set. Neither pin is in the Klipper config, so under Kalico they float.
  • Driving PB1 alone did not help. PB7 is the hotend heater power enable: with PB7 high the heater went from 24 to 62 °C in 15 s and held 60.
  • firmwareExe's host GPIOs (gpio_out) are only used by doPowerOff, printCompletedPowerOff and sLightCheck, not for the heaters.
  • The stock mainboard firmware only has PC0 (the load cell level_res) as a fixed output.
  • The bed heater works under Kalico unchanged: M140 S50 took the bed from 25 to 34 °C in 30 s at max_power 0.4, with no extra power pin.

The config that fixes it:

[static_digital_output eboard_power]
pins: eboard:PB1        # stock keeps it high

[output_pin heater_power]
pin: eboard:PB7
value: 1
shutdown_value: 0       # shutdown cuts heater power

items.title: pcb_fan
items.text:
[fan_generic pcb_fan] on PA5 stays off until SET_FAN_SPEED is sent. Under Kalico nothing sent it, and the Y TMC2209 shut down on over-temperature (ot=1 t120) in the middle of a print.

  • Stock firmwareExe sends SET_FAN_SPEED FAN=pcb_fan SPEED=1 in SerialObject::serialPrint before M24, and SPEED=0 in its end and cancel cleanup. It also sends 1 and then 0 in FourToOne::changeStart (an IFS change), Filament::dryingStart and auto calibration, and there is a manual toggle in More Info.
  • There is no SoC temperature to drive it: the X2600 kernel has no thermal or hwmon driver, and stock never read one.
  • The Kalico printer.base.cfg uses [controller_fan pcb_fan] with pin: PA5 and heater: extruder (all steppers by default). The fan is on while any motor is enabled or the hotend heats, and off 30 s after idle. That covers prints, IFS changes and cancels, like stock.

items.title: Clock
items.text: All three boards (mainboard, eboard and IFS) use the same clock set-up.

items.title: Stock
items.text:
The Nations SDK SystemInit is the same in all three firmwares:

  • HSE on, CFGR &= 0xf7c0ffff; CFGR |= 0x081f0000: PLL source HSE, HSE/2, PLLMULFCT 0x17 = x24. The 12 MHz crystal gives 144 MHz.
  • CFGR |= 0x2000 | 0x500: APB2 /2 (72 MHz) and APB1 /4 (36 MHz).
  • Flash latency 4.
  • Without HSE, SystemCoreClock is 8000000 (HSI).

items.title: The problem in Kalico
items.text:
kalico-ad5x's N32G45x support uses the generic STM32F1 clock_setup() (src/stm32/stm32f1.c), and CLOCK_FREQ is fixed at 128 MHz for the N32G45x (no prompt in Kconfig):

  • With STM32_CLOCK_REF_12M the divider is 128/6 = 21, which is above 16, so it is halved to 10. HSE x10 is 120 MHz, while Kalico assumes 128 MHz, which is a timing error of about 6.7%.
  • It also sets flash latency 2 and APB1 /2, where stock uses 4 and /4.

items.title: The fix
items.text:
Mainline Klipper has its own N32G45x clock code in src/stm32/stm32f1.c (the N32 power register PWR_BASE + 0x0c, flash latency from the clock, APB /4 above a limit) and a default of 144000000 for the N32G45x in Kconfig. With a 12 MHz crystal it uses a divider of 24 and HSE x12, which is 144 MHz.

kalico-ad5x carries that clock code and the 144 MHz default for all three boards. The IFS build also drops to HSI and stops the PLL before reconfiguring, like the stock SystemInit.

Checked on the mainboard: Moonraker reports CLOCK_FREQ 144000000 and a measured frequency of 144000685. Without the patch it would have been about 120 MHz.

items.title: Flashing and test builds
items.text: The three boards are flashed differently. The IFS has its own page: see Kalico firmware on the IFS.

items.title: Flashing from the installer
items.text:
The installer flashes the images in mcu-firmware/ad5x in the AD5X-FS clone (AD5X-mainboard.bin, AD5X-ifs.hex, AD5X-eboard.hex, with SHA256SUMS and VERSION). common/flash-mcu-firmware.sh checks every file against SHA256SUMS, skips the step when all three boards already report the commit in VERSION, and runs ad5x-mcu-flash on the folder:

  • the mainboard with NationsCommand on ttyS2, judged by "verification succeeded" in its log
  • the IFS live, as described in Kalico firmware on the IFS (including an IFS that still runs FlashForge's firmware)
  • the eboard by copying the hex to /usr/data/kalico-fw and writing its path into eboard.flash, so 08-mcu-wake.sh flashes it at the next real power-on (a reboot is not enough, because the bootloader only waits after power-on)

It refuses to run during a print or a pause, pauses Klippy while it flashes and restarts it afterwards, and logs to /usr/data/logs/mcu-flash.log.

items.title: Mainboard
items.text:
NationsCommand is the Nations N32 ISP over the chip's ROM bootloader on /dev/ttyS2. It toggles BOOT0 and RESET through host GPIOs (/sys/class/gpio); the GPIO numbers are not known yet. Recovery is always possible from the host, with no SWD needed.

cd /usr/prog/PROGRAM/control/1.1.1
./NationsCommand -c -d --fn /usr/data/kalico-fw/mainboard.bin --v -r

A flash shows the ISP at 9600 baud, BOOT Command Version V22, SubVersion V25 and the chip UID, then erase all, download, "Chip verification succeeded" and a reset. NationsCommand also deletes the 0-byte UpdateM file in its own folder.

Start FlashForge's own Klipper with /usr/prog/klipper/start.sh, never with klipperDaemon start directly: start.sh sets LD_LIBRARY_PATH for FlashForge's Python, and without it Klippy dies at once without writing a log.

Way back to stock: the same command with /usr/prog/PROGRAM/control/1.1.1/AD5X.bin (md5 522b4641821016952cd4504e4c2177ed).

items.title: Eboard
items.text:
The eboard has FlashForge's IAP bootloader at 0x08000000 to 0x0800FFFF, and the app at 0x08010000.

  • Plain reset: the bootloader stays in IAP mode, waiting on ttyS5 at 115200 and printing Ready lines. An A (0x41) is answered with ACK (0x06) and it starts the app. This is what eboard_start in 08-mcu-wake.sh does (the previous boot's startup.sh did the same).
  • BKP->DR1 = 0x1234 and a reset: the bootloader skips IAP and starts the app at once. The stock code does it as: PWR and BKP clocks on, PWR_CR.DBP through bit-band 0x420E0020, BKP->DR1 = 0x1234 at 0x40006C00 + 4, then NVIC_SystemReset(). This is used for Klipper's reset command.
  • The bootloader does not start an app whose initial stack pointer is 0x20010000 (64 KiB RAM). Stock and kiln-os use 0x20020000.

IAPCommand ("stm32isp") is stm32isp [Options] <file> <comport> <baudrate>, with -verbose. It reads Intel hex, uses /sys/class/gpio (probably the eboard reset), and deletes /usr/prog/PROGRAM/control/Update when it runs.

The eboard can only be flashed while its bootloader waits after power-on, before eboard_start sends A:

  • IAPCommand -verbose eboard.hex /dev/ttyS5 against a running app fails with "Can not connect to board, timed-out", and nothing is written.
  • A Klipper reset sent to the stock app does not help either: the stock app resets with the BKP DR1 bypass and goes straight back into the app.

So the flash is done by a boot hook in 08-mcu-wake.sh (stock FlashForge also flashes the eboard at boot, in run.sh).

items.title: The boot hook
items.text:
In eboard_start, after Ready:

  1. If /usr/data/kalico-fw/eboard.flash exists, read the hex path from it and delete the file.
  2. Run IAPCommand <hex> /dev/ttyS5, logging to /usr/data/logs/openad5x/eboard-flash.log.
  3. Reopen ttyS5 and go round the loop again (A if the bootloader still waits, "application already running" if not).

A successful run logs eboard: flashing ..., eboard: IAPCommand exit 0 and eboard: application started, and the flash log shows 36 frames, STM32Write: success. and STM32iap finished NA..

Way back to stock:

echo /usr/prog/PROGRAM/control/1.1.1/ADM_App.hex > /usr/data/kalico-fw/eboard.flash

then reboot.

items.title: What the printer shows after flashing
items.text:
With only the MCUs on Kalico and FlashForge's Klipper still on the host, Klipper reports "MCU Protocol error" and lists both MCUs with the Kalico versions. The cause is mcu 'eboard': Unable to extract params from: config_lis2dw: FlashForge's [lis2dw] host module sends an older config_lis2dw than Kalico's firmware. This is expected and goes away once Kalico runs on the host.

With the mainboard on Kalico and the stock host, Klipper loads 137 commands (stock: 116) and 1024 moves (stock: 4096), and reaches ready with no protocol error.

items.title: Test builds
items.text: Builds are made in WSL with make 4.4.1 and the Arm GNU Toolchain 14.2.rel1. The build script copies kalico-ad5x to a scratch folder and converts the copy to LF (the Windows checkout is CRLF, and make needs LF), copies in the board's .config, then runs make olddefconfig and make. The repository itself is never touched. A version string ending in -dirty comes from that LF conversion.

Built from kalico-eboard.config: klipper.bin 37512 B, and klipper.hex made with arm-none-eabi-objcopy -O ihex klipper.elf.

Ours kiln-os eboard.hex Stock ADM_App.hex Load address 0x08010000 0x08010000 0x08010000 Size 37512 41428 36012 SP 0x20020000 0x20020000 0x20020000 CLOCK_FREQ / baud 144 MHz / 230400 same same Hex records type 4 0x0801, 16-byte data, type 5, EOF, CRLF same same (some 8 and 12-byte records)

The disassembly of command_reset shows the PWR and BKP clocks on (RCC+0x1c |= 0x18000000), PWR_CR |= DBP, BKP(0x40006C00)+4 = 0x1234, DBP off, then NVIC_SystemReset.

items.title: FlashForge's host-side changes
items.text:
firmwareExe opens ttyS2, ttyS3, ttyS4 (IFS), ttyS5 and ttyS7 (load cell).

FlashForge replaced these Klippy files in the 3.1.6 software package:

File What it adds query_adc.py QUERY_ADC, GET_FILAMENT_VALUE, GET_CUT_VALUE (eboard PA3 and PA2) virtual_sdcard.py SDCARD_CLEAR_REFUELLING, SDCARD_SET_CHANNEL, SDCARD_ENABLE_FFM (IFS print integration with firmwareExe) extruder.py, exclude_object.py Modified versions

There is also an extra module, extras/bl24c16f.py (EEPROM).

items.title: Kalico's Klippy on the AD5X
items.text:
• CPU: Ingenic X2600, mips32r2, NaN2008, FP64. glibc 2.33 (rootfs lib/ld-2.33.so, lib/libc-2.33.so, /lib/ld-linux-mipsn8.so.1). The stock printer has no compiler.
  • FlashForge's Python is /usr/prog/Python-3.8.2. Moonraker already runs on it.
  • The Kalico source is kalico-ad5x (FlashForge-C5-Modding-Group, from KalicoCrew upstream).

items.title: Python version
items.text:
Klippy from kalico-ad5x does not start on Python 3.8:

  • pyproject.toml says requires-python = ">=3.9".
  • printer.py calls compat.install() on every start, and that uses str.removeprefix (3.9 and later) in compat.py.
  • configfile.py also uses removeprefix (for Python script config values), and some extras use runtime list[...] and tuple[...] annotations without from __future__ import annotations: extras/nozzle_cleanup.py, extras/probe_eddy_current.py, extras/load_cell/ads1220.py and extras/load_cell/hx71x.py.

So the host needs Python 3.9 or newer, built for mips32r2, NaN2008 and FP64, or Klippy would have to be patched for 3.8. OpenAD5X uses the first option: the hard-float Python 3.13 build described below, installed as described in Entware and Python.

items.title: The Python 3.13 hard-float build
items.text:
From the opencreator-fs release python-3.13-hardfloat-r2 (2026-10-16), asset python-hf-c5-release.zip (which unpacks to python-hf-c5.tar.gz). It is "meant only for FlashForge devices, such as the Creator 5/Pro and AD5X".

  • Contents (BUILDINFO-c5): Python 3.13.9 with prefix /usr/data/python-hf, numpy 2.2.2, greenlet 3.3.2 and cffi 2.0.0. Built with the Ingenic MIPS GCC 12.1 Release 6.0.0 toolchain (xburst2, glibc 2.33), from the C5's Kalico fork at commit 3250f3bff229276f52a5e4c2d0ce1c09b8fc0ddb. The AD5X uses kalico-ad5x, not that fork.
  • ABI: bin/python3.13 has flags 0x70001405, NaN2008, FP64, and interpreter /lib/ld-linux-mipsn8.so.1, the same as firmwareExe. lib/libpython3.13.so.1.0 needs up to GLIBC_2.33, which matches the AD5X rootfs.
  • Packages: cffi, greenlet, jinja2, markupsafe, numpy, pycparser, serial (pyserial) and dbus_fast: all the Kalico host packages.
  • Own libraries: libffi, libssl and libcrypto 3, libsqlite3, liblzma, libbz2, libjpeg, libsodium, libatomic and libgcc_s.
  • cc/bin/gcc: a shell wrapper around Entware's gcc (${ENTWARE_GCC:-/opt/bin/gcc}). It adds -mabi=32 -mips32r2 -mhard-float -mfp64 -mnan=2008 and the bundled glibc headers and crt files (cc/lib, cc/include), so Klippy can build c_helper.so on the printer. It needs Entware's gcc in /opt.

items.title: c_helper.so
items.text:
klippy/chelper/__init__.py get_ffi() compiles c_helper.so with gcc on the first start, and again whenever the C sources are newer than the .so (check_build_code). The sources are pyhelper.c serialqueue.c stepcompress.c steppersync.c itersolve.c trapq.c pollreactor.c plus the kinematics files in SOURCE_FILES.

With Entware's gcc and the wrapper above, the printer builds it itself in about 46 s (305 KB, NaN2008, FP64). Without a compiler it would have to be cross-built (glibc, mips32r2, NaN2008, FP64, -Wall -g -O2 -shared -fPIC) and shipped with a newer modification time than the sources.

items.title: Python packages
items.text:
This is why FlashForge's own Python 3.8.2 cannot be used for Kalico, even apart from the version check:

Package Kalico (Python below 3.12) FlashForge has cffi 1.15.1 1.13.1 greenlet 2.0.2 3.0.3 Jinja2 3.1.6 or newer 2.10.3 and 3.1.2 (3.1.2 may come from ZMod, the dump is from a ZMod printer) markupsafe 2.1.5 1.1.1 and 2.1.1 (the same caveat) numpy about 2.0 (Python 3.9) 1.16.4 pyserial 3.4 3.4

With a newer Python these packages have to be built for it too: cffi, greenlet, markupsafe and numpy have C parts. The python-hf build includes them. The FlashForge packages are in the factory image at usr/prog/Python-3.8.2/lib/python3.8/site-packages.

items.title: Build configs
items.text:
The Kalico build configs are in AD5X-FS, under mcu-firmware/ad5x/config/:

File Board Settings kalico-mainboard.config Mainboard N32G455, no bootloader (STM32_FLASH_START_0000), 12 MHz crystal, USART1 on PA10/PA9, 230400 kalico-eboard.config Eboard The same, with the 64 KiB bootloader (STM32_FLASH_START_10000) kalico-ifs.config IFS N32G455, 64 KiB bootloader, 12 MHz, USART1, 115200, STM32_FLASHFORGE_IFS

items.title: Patches in kalico-ad5x
items.text:
1. Clock: mainline Klipper's N32G45x clock code and the 144 MHz default, for all three boards. See Clock.
  2. RAM size: RAM_SIZE of 128 KiB for the N32G455, because the eboard bootloader checks the stack pointer. The IFS uses 0x8000 (SP 0x20008000) instead; stock IFS has an SP of 0x20007498.
  3. Eboard reset: command_reset sets BKP->DR1 = 0x1234 and resets, and bootloader_request is a plain reset.
  4. IFS bootloader request: erase page 0x0800D000 and reset, so the IFS can be reflashed over its serial port. See Kalico firmware on the IFS.
  5. IFS RS485: direction control on PA11 and the half-duplex link. See the same page.

items.title: FlashForge-only MCU commands
items.text:
These exist in FlashForge's stock firmware and are not in Kalico:

  • Mainboard and Exboard: board identification strings, used by the stock checkEboard
  • set_radar_interval and set_radar_sync_pulse: purpose unknown ("radar")
  • i2c_modify_bits, i2c_set_software_bus and spi_set_software_bus: older Klipper bus commands

items.title: kiln-os
items.text:
kiln-os (GPL-3.0) is open firmware for the AD5X: mainline Klipper, Linux 6.6, a recovery OS and one-click updates. Its klipper/ folder was a useful reference:

  • Both boards are flashed with mainline Klipper v0.13.0-803-g4cd711119.
  • mcu-configs/ad5x-mainboard.config uses MACH_N32G455xE (from the xblax/klipper Kconfig), CLOCK_FREQ=144000000, STM32_CLOCK_REF_12M, STM32_FLASH_START_0000, USART1, 230400 and RAM_SIZE=0x20000. ad5x-eboard.config is the same with MACH_N32G455xC and STM32_FLASH_START_10000. So both boards are N32G455 (mainboard xE, eboard xC).
  • mcu-patches/ against mainline Klipper:
    • 0001 (xblax): command_reset on the N32G455 with a 64 KiB bootloader writes BKP->DR1 = 0x1234 and resets (bootloader bypass, which fixes FIRMWARE_RESTART).
    • 0002 (xblax): bootloader_request on the N32G455 with a 64 KiB bootloader is a plain NVIC_SystemReset() (the bootloader stays in IAP by default).
    • 0003: RAM_SIZE 0x20000 for the N32G455, because the eboard bootloader checks the stack pointer.
  • It also has an IFS module (klipper/extras/ifs.py, ifs.cfg) that keeps the stock IFS firmware and translates to F-commands over ttyS4. OpenAD5X replaces the IFS firmware instead. A host-side patch, patches/trsync-timeout-50ms.patch, is included too.

items.title: Open items
items.text: What is still unknown or not done on the MCU and host side.

items.title: Mainboard
items.text:
• The host GPIO numbers NationsCommand uses for the mainboard's BOOT0 and RESET. They could come from the tool's code or from an strace on the printer.
  • kalico-ad5x has no MACH_N32G455xE or xC sub-variants (those come from xblax/klipper). What they change compared with the plain MACH_N32G455 has not been checked.
  • What the FlashForge-only set_radar_* commands are used for.

items.title: Load cell
items.text: • Weighing and crash detection through the load cell on ttyS7 are not implemented. Probing works: the trigger is a plain pin (PB3), and the load cell is tared and read with H1 and H7. See Bed load cell.

items.title: Host
items.text: • The stock printer's Jinja2 and MarkupSafe versions without ZMod are not known (the dump comes from a ZMod printer).

items.title: Moved elsewhere
items.text:
These were open earlier and are done:

  • Host Python, Entware, the compiler, the c_helper.so build and the boot script that sets the NaN byte and the /opt mount: see Entware and Python.
  • ttyS3: unused air-quality sensor code from another model, see Power key.

The IFS open questions are on IFS hardware.

items.title: firmwareExe: filament change
items.text: What the stock firmwareExe 3.1.6 does for a filament change, from its decompile, and how the AFC settings map to it. Source paths in the binary are ../ad5x/serial/SerialObject.cpp. It is a MIPS32 ELF, not stripped, with debug info.

items.title: Settings (/usr/data/config/Adventurer5M.json)

items.title: Toolhead filament sensor (SerialObject::checkFilamentSenser)
items.text:
• GET_FILAMENT_VALUE (stock query_adc.py, eboard PA3 read as a "temperature" ADC), present when value <= 0.3 || value >= 0.72
  • Kalico: QUERY_ADC NAME='temperature_sensor filamentValue' read 0.319 with no filament in the toolhead (cut sensor PA2: 0.508)

items.title: Change (SerialObject::changeChannel)
items.text:
1. M400, M114 (save X/Y), G1 Z(z+5) (or Z220 if z > 220), M400
  2. doLoadAndUnload(new, old):
  3. cutFilament(old) when the toolhead sensor shows filament, else checkCrotchCutting
  4. IFS F11 C<old> ... 1200 (unload), checkRefulling, then IFS feed of the new lane (F10-type, up to 650 mm at 1200 mm/min) until checkFeeding / the toolhead sensor
  5. wait for nozzle temperature, getFlushVol (from the two lane colours, calc_flush_vol)
  6. cleanFilamentBox once, twice when flush volume > 400
  7. SET_FAN_SPEED FAN=fanM106 SPEED=.., G1 Y<saved>, M400, G1 X<saved>, M400, G1 Z<saved>, M400, G92 E<saved>, SDCARD_CLEAR_REFUELLING

AFC Value Stock pin_loc_xy / pin_park_dist / cut_move_dist 14.0, -5.6 / 6 / 14.8 park X20, cut to X-0.8 at Y-5.6 z_hop (AFC.cfg) 5 G1 Z(z+5) kick (AFC.cfg) False none tool_stn_unload / tool_unload_speed 60 / 10 UnloadESpace / UnloadSpeed toolhead sensor [ad5x_filament_sensor fill_sensor] + u1_filament_sensor_name: fill_sensor eboard PA3, 0.3 / 0.72
