items.title: Cut
items.text:
• checkCrotchCutting(chn): IFS F24 C<chn> (turn the selector to that lane and clamp it), poll until the IFS state is 5 (ready); state 0x7f (homing error) -> F15 re-home and retry. AFC does the same with select_lane before every lane move, nothing extra needed
  • ADX_CUT (in AFC_IFS.py, set as AFC's tool_cut_cmd) does the stock cut itself: G1 Y10 F18000, G1 Y<pin_y> F1800 at the current X, G1 X<pin_x + pin_park_dist> F12000, G1 X<pin_x - cut_move_dist> F600, then G1 E-5 F600. Positions come from _AFC_CUT_TIP_VARS

items.title: Kalico on the AD5X host
items.text:
How Klippy from kalico-ad5x is installed on the printer: on Python 3.13 (/usr/data/python-hf), talking to the Kalico mainboard and eboard, with Moonraker, Fluidd and GrumpyScreen as before.

FlashForge's own Klipper (/usr/prog/klipper) and its config stay untouched, so going back is one switch.

Previous layout

This page is the by-hand install on the test printer, with Kalico in /usr/data/kalico and its config in /usr/data/config/kalico. The installer puts the same things under /usr/data/openad5x/klipper; see Files on the printer. The approach follows OpenCreator's touchscreen-installer (payload-template/soc/install-stack.sh) and opencreator-fs (startup/scripts/10-klipper.sh): the same Python bundle and the same Kalico-on-host idea.

items.title: What has to be in place first
items.text:
What Where Python 3.13.9 hard-float /usr/data/python-hf Entware with gcc, and the empty specs file renamed /usr/data/bin/opt, mounted on /opt at boot by startup.d/05-entware.sh The c_helper.so build the python-hf cc/bin/gcc wrapper and /opt/bin/gcc Mainboard and eboard firmware built from the same kalico-ad5x commit as the host checkout ttyS2 and ttyS5 Moonraker /usr/data/moonraker, started with -d /usr/data: config in /usr/data/config, logs in /usr/data/logs, gcodes in /usr/data/gcodes, klippy_uds_address: /tmp/uds

See Entware and Python and Flashing.

items.title: Layout
items.text:
Path What /usr/data/kalico/klipper The kalico-ad5x checkout (git, shallow) /usr/data/kalico/klippy-env python-hf -m venv --without-pip --system-site-packages /usr/data/kalico/start.sh Starts Klippy in a loop (like OpenCreator's 10-klipper.sh) /usr/data/config/kalico/printer.cfg and its includes The Kalico config, in Moonraker's config root so Fluidd can edit it /usr/data/logs/klippy.log The Kalico log (stock keeps printer.log) /tmp/uds The API socket, the same as stock, so Moonraker needs no change

These stock files are left as they are: /usr/prog/klipper/, /usr/data/config/printer.cfg and /usr/data/config/printer.base.cfg.

items.title: 1. Git from Entware
items.text:
export PATH=/opt/bin:/opt/sbin:$PATH
opkg update
opkg install git git-http ca-bundle

This installs git 2.50.1 and leaves 1.6 GB free on /usr/data.

items.title: 2. The Kalico checkout
items.text:
mkdir -p /usr/data/kalico
git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/FlashForge-C5-Modding-Group/kalico-ad5x.git /usr/data/kalico/klipper
git -C /usr/data/kalico/klipper rev-parse --short HEAD

The checkout is about 260 MB, most of it lib/ (the MCU vendor SDKs). It must be the same commit the MCU firmware was built from.

items.title: 3. The virtual environment and c_helper.so
items.text:
/usr/data/python-hf/bin/python3.13 -m venv --without-pip --system-site-packages /usr/data/kalico/klippy-env
cd /usr/data/kalico/klipper/klippy
PATH=/usr/data/python-hf/cc/bin:/opt/bin:$PATH /usr/data/kalico/klippy-env/bin/python -c 'import chelper; chelper.get_ffi()'

pyvenv.cfg ends up with home = /usr/data/python-hf/bin, include-system-site-packages = true and version = 3.13.9. klippy/chelper/c_helper.so is about 305 KB, flags 0x70001407 (nan2008, mips32r2).

Klippy rebuilds c_helper.so on start when the chelper sources are newer, for example after a Kalico update. That needs the same PATH (python-hf cc/bin and /opt/bin) and /opt mounted.

items.title: 4. The config: stock, copied
items.text:
mkdir -p /usr/data/config/kalico
cp /usr/data/config/printer.cfg /usr/data/config/printer.base.cfg /usr/data/config/kalico/

This takes the printer's own files, with its calibration (bed mesh, PID, input shaper). Stock keeps using the originals.

items.title: 5. The start script
items.text:
/usr/data/kalico/start.sh:

#!/bin/sh
# Kalico klippy on python-hf, restarts after exit
export PATH=/usr/data/python-hf/cc/bin:$PATH:/opt/bin
K=/usr/data/kalico
cd /
while true; do
    $K/klippy-env/bin/python $K/klipper/klippy/klippy.py /usr/data/config/kalico/printer.cfg \
        -l /usr/data/logs/klippy.log -a /tmp/uds >> /usr/data/logs/klippy.out 2>&1 < /dev/null
    sleep 3
done

startup.sh starts it with setsid when it is executable, and otherwise starts the stock Klipper. Entware must be mounted before Klippy needs a compiler, which is only after a Kalico update. klippy_restart.sh stops every Klippy (stock and Kalico) and lets the loop start one again.

items.title: 6. Starting by hand
items.text:
To try it without rebooting, stop stock Klipper and start Klippy yourself:

/usr/prog/klipper/klipperDaemon stop
PATH=/usr/data/python-hf/cc/bin:$PATH:/opt/bin nohup /usr/data/kalico/klippy-env/bin/python \
  /usr/data/kalico/klipper/klippy/klippy.py /usr/data/config/kalico/printer.cfg \
  -l /usr/data/logs/klippy.log -a /tmp/uds > /usr/data/logs/klippy.out 2>&1 &

Moonraker connects by itself, because klippy_uds_address is already /tmp/uds.

items.title: Config changes from stock
items.text:
All the stock sections exist in Kalico (bed_mesh display_status exclude_object extruder fan_generic force_move gcode_arcs gcode_macro heater_bed heater_fan idle_timeout input_shaper led lis2dw mcu pause_resume pid_calibrate printer probe resonance_tester stepper_x/y/z temperature_sensor tmc2209 verify_heater virtual_sdcard). What changes:

Stock Change [printer] max_accel_to_decel: 5000 Kalico reports Option 'max_accel_to_decel' is not valid in section 'printer'. Replace it with minimum_cruise_ratio: 0.75 (20000 x (1 - 0.75) = 5000, the same as stock) [virtual_sdcard] path /usr/data/gcodes, the same as stock FlashForge-only commands (QUERY_ADC, GET_FILAMENT_VALUE, GET_CUT_VALUE, SDCARD_SET_CHANNEL, ...) They come from FlashForge's own klippy files, so they do not exist in Kalico. The filamentValue and cutValue sensors stay as temperature_sensor (Generic 3950 on eboard PA3 and PA2) Macros M900 M106 M107 HOME MYG67 M900, M106 and M107 kept; HOME and MYG67 removed Calibration Taken over from the printer's own /usr/data/config/printer.cfg: z_offset, bed mesh, PID, input shaper

The fix for the first error is sed -i '137s/^max_accel_to_decel:5000$/minimum_cruise_ratio: 0.75/' /usr/data/config/kalico/printer.base.cfg, then a Moonraker POST /printer/restart.

The load cell commands are added through macros.cfg, included from printer.cfg. See Load cell in Kalico. A test entry [output_pin level_res] pin: PC0 (stock drives PC0 high at boot) is not needed for the load cell.

items.title: What a good start looks like
items.text:
• Klippy is ready, with no other config errors or warnings in klippy.log.
  • Moonraker's /printer/info shows software_version as the checkout commit and python_path as /usr/data/kalico/klippy-env/bin/python.
  • Each MCU logs Loaded MCU '...' 137 commands (Kalico v2026.10.00-...) and Configured MCU '...' (1024 moves). The measured clocks were 144000698 Hz for the mainboard and 144000659 Hz for the eboard.
  • Stock's config_lis2dw protocol error is gone.
  • The MCU builds say -dirty when they were built from a CRLF-to-LF converted copy on a PC.

items.title: Going back to stock
items.text:
1. Host: stop Kalico, start stock with /usr/prog/klipper/start.sh, and disable /usr/data/kalico/start.sh (chmod -x or rename it, then reboot).
  2. Mainboard: NationsCommand -c -d --fn /usr/prog/PROGRAM/control/1.1.1/AD5X.bin --v -r
  3. Eboard: echo /usr/prog/PROGRAM/control/1.1.1/ADM_App.hex > /usr/data/kalico-fw/eboard.flash, then power-cycle.

items.title: Open
items.text:
• Where Kalico's printer.cfg should live: /usr/data/config/kalico/ (now) or replacing the stock printer.cfg.
  • Whether to get Kalico through Entware's git (now) or copy a checkout from a PC with pscp.
  • A Moonraker update manager for Kalico. There is none on purpose: [update_manager] is left out of moonraker.conf.

items.title: Load cell in Kalico
items.text:
How Kalico probes and levels with the AD5X bed load cell. The board and its protocol are on Bed load cell.

The trigger is a plain [probe] on PB3, which the board drives itself. Kalico only has to tare the board before probing, with H1 and H7 on ttyS7. There is no [load_cell] section, so Kalico's own load cell command names are free and are used as macros.

items.title: Commands
items.text: Command What it does LOAD_CELL_TARE H1, then H7; succeeds when the reading is below 31 g, up to 10 tries LOAD_CELL_READ H7: shows grams and the raw count LOAD_CELL_DIAGNOSTIC [COUNT=10] Reads H7 several times and shows min, max and spread LOAD_CELL_CALIBRATE Not mapped (H2 changes the factory calibration)

items.title: Files
items.text: File What /usr/data/openad5x/loadcell/loadcell.sh Sends the H commands over ttyS7 at 9600 baud, the way stock sendCmdToUart7 does: up to 5 tries, a reply is complete when it is longer than 12 bytes and contains ok macros.cfg [gcode_shell_command loadcell] (timeout 60, verbose: True), the three commands above and the wrappers below

items.title: Tare before probing
items.text:
Stock tares with the nozzle off the bed before every probe session. macros.cfg does the same with _LOAD_CELL_PREPARE: save state, G90, G1 Z5 F800, restore state, M400, LOAD_CELL_TARE. The probe commands are renamed and wrapped so they call it first:

Command Wrapper PROBE _LOAD_CELL_PREPARE, then _PROBE_BASE PROBE_ACCURACY _LOAD_CELL_PREPARE, then _PROBE_ACCURACY_BASE PROBE_CALIBRATE _LOAD_CELL_PREPARE, then _PROBE_CALIBRATE_BASE BED_MESH_CALIBRATE _LOAD_CELL_PREPARE, then _BED_MESH_CALIBRATE_BASE

items.title: Homing Z
items.text: G28 is renamed G28.1. After a Z home (a plain G28, or one that names Z), _HOME_Z_PROBE runs when X and Y are homed: G1 Z10 F1500, G1 X107.5 Y107.5 F12000, PROBE HOME=Z, G1 Z5 F800. The bed touch is then Z0. Without X and Y homed, Z homes to the switch only.

items.title: Results
items.text:
• The probe read -3.26 in the switch coordinates.
  • After PROBE HOME=Z, a probe at the bed centre reads about -0.011.
  • [probe] z_offset is -0.25, as stock. The mesh reads about -3.0 against the touch at -3.26. The first layer is still to be verified.
  • Old meshes carry the -3.2 frame and must not be loaded.

items.title: Limits
items.text:
• RUN_SHELL_COMMAND ignores the script's exit code, so a failed tare does not stop a probe by itself.
  • A [probe] activate_gcode cannot move, which is why the tare is in wrappers and not in the probe section.
  • "Probe samples exceed samples_tolerance" appears when the board still has an old zero.
  • Starting a probe with the nozzle on the bed gives "Probe triggered prior to movement".

items.title: Bed load cell
items.text: How the bed probe works without FlashForge's firmwareExe, so Kalico can level and probe. How Kalico uses it is on Load cell in Kalico.

items.title: Hardware
items.text:
The spare part is sold as "Flashforge AD5X Pressure leveling sensor (Strain Gauge)" (West3D SKU ELE4358).

  • Load cells: 4 strain-gauge cells (U-cut plates), labelled 739 H, 734 X, 736 X and 730 H, 3-wire (half bridges). J6, J8, J3 and J7 are cells A, B, C and D.
  • Board: silkscreen "GUAGE-SENSOR" (FlashForge wiki photo "electronic scale"):
    • U4: a 16-pin SOP HX711, with DOUT on pin 12 and PD_SCK on pin 11. Kalico supports it ([load_cell] and [load_cell_probe] with sensor_type: hx711).
    • U7: an STC8G1K08A (SOP-8, 8051 core, 8 KB flash). Its pins are P5.4/RST, VCC, P5.5, GND, P3.0 RxD, P3.1 TxD, P3.2 and P3.3.
    • J9 "ISP": VCC, RX, TX, GND. This is the STC's UART programming header: the ROM bootloader listens on P3.0 and P3.1 for 0x7F at every power-on.
    • K2: a button (reset or tare).
    • J1: 5-pin, to the mainboard.
  • No firmware for this board is in FlashForge's packages, and firmwareExe has no update code for it (only H1, H7, H2 and H3). STC's ISP has no flash read, so the stock firmware cannot be dumped. There is no Klipper or Kalico support for an 8051.
  • Reading the HX711 directly would let Kalico tare and probe without the H commands. It needs either Kalico running on the STC (unlikely for an 8051) or the HX711 DOUT and SCK wired to free pins on a Kalico MCU, which is a hardware mod.

items.title: Mainboard side
items.text:
J23 "LEVEL" is 6 pins: VCC RX TX RES DET GND (mainboard FFP0302_Main_Board_V3.0.0). The board side is J1, also 6-pin.

Pin Goes to RX, TX The STC's UART, to the SoC's ttyS7 DET The trigger, to the mainboard N32 PB3 ([probe]) RES Reset line to the STC. firmwareExe never drives it, and it is not in the stock Klipper config. Where it ends is unknown (an unused N32 pin, an unused SoC GPIO, or nowhere). It needs a multimeter or trace check

The stock mainboard firmware drives PC0 itself. It sets PC0 high in its init, and a pulse generator then sets and clears it from counters, which fits the FlashForge MCU command set_radar_sync_pulse. PC0 is in no stock config section, and Kalico leaves it as an input. It looked like a candidate for RES, but tests showed it is not (below).

items.title: What the board does
items.text:
Tested on a real board, over ttyS7 at 9600 baud, with a command plus \n and a 1.5 s read:

  • H7 replies command H7 ok. 8840174 -520 g: the raw count and then the weight in grams. A board that was not tared reads about -520 g with nothing on the bed.
  • H1 replies command H1 ok. 8839484 (the raw count only). H1 tares: a following H7 reads 0 g.
  • Raw noise is a few hundred counts between reads, about 0.5 g.
  • Nothing is sent unasked: listening for 4 s at 115200, 230400 and 9600 gave 0 bytes.
  • PC0 is not the STC reset. Pulling PC0 low for 100 ms did not tare or reset the board (a tared 0 g stayed 0 g). Holding PC0 low for about 3 s and reading H7 during it, the STC kept answering. PC0, the stock "radar sync pulse" output, goes somewhere else.
  • QUERY_PROBE under Kalico reads "not triggered" with nothing on the bed. The board drives PB3 by itself, so no command is needed for a trigger.
  • If RES can be driven from the printer, the STC could be flashed over ttyS7 without an adapter (reset plus 0x7F, stcgal).

items.title: Protocol (from the firmwareExe 3.1.6 decompile)
items.text:
• Port: /dev/ttyS7, 9600 baud (cfsetispeed and cfsetospeed with 0xd, B9600). The IFS port, ttyS4, is opened at B115200.
  • Format: Serial("/dev/ttyS7", "~", "\n"). A command is sent as the text plus \n. The ~ probably ends a reply.
  • sendCmdToUart7: flush, send, read the reply, up to 5 tries. A reply is complete when it has more than 12 bytes and contains ok, and stock waits up to 1 s for more bytes.
  • Commands:
Command What it does H1 Zero (tare). Also the H1 Point button in the WeightAdjust screen H7 Read the value. The reply is split at spaces: field 4 is the raw count, field 5 the grams H2 S500 Calibrate with 500 g (WeightAdjust, bed at 60 °C, Z 100). It changes the factory calibration, so do not send it H3 S200, H3 S100 Check with 200 g or 100 g. Not confirmed on hardware, do not send
  • SerialObject::checkLevelPinStatus(): up to 10 times, send H1, then H7, and take field 4. It succeeds when the absolute value is below 31 and fails after 10 tries ("Level probe can not clear").
  • It is called from Print::doPreparation (before every print), Print::checkZ, GuiderLevelPrint::doLevel, Settings::doLevel and WeightAdjust::on_H1_clicked.

So stock tares the load cell before every print, Z check and levelling, and the probe itself is plain Klipper [probe] on PB3.

items.title: Stock levelling
items.text:
• Commands: plain Klipper ones: G28 Z, BED_MESH_CALIBRATE, PROBE_CALIBRATE, SET_GCODE_OFFSET Z=, BED_MESH_PROFILE SAVE=MESH_DATA and LOAD=MESH_DATA, SAVE_CONFIG.
  • Errors shown: "Level probe can not clear.", "Leveling sensor data cannot be cleared.", "Level probe no trigger.", "Leveling sensor not triggered.", "Leveling sensor triggered early." and "Abnormal leveling data".
  • A failed tare cancels the print: the mesh is dropped and the heaters, fan and motors are turned off, with "Leveling sensor cannot be cleared. Please check the sensor." If no board answers, the reading parses as 0 and the check passes.

items.title: The check before every print (Print::checkZ)
items.text:
1. Home Z (max endstop), X and Y. Purge box, heat, purge 90 mm, wipe.
  2. Z5, X60 Y-3, tare, PROBE_CALIBRATE and ABORT (this gives z1).
  3. Scrub the front edge (z1 + 0.3, X130 to X150, z1 + 0.1).
  4. Bed centre X107.5 Y107.5, tare, probe (z2).
  5. The difference is z2 minus the saved centre Z. SET_GCODE_OFFSET Z=<diff> MOVE=1 is sent if it is between -0.5 and 2.0.
  6. BED_MESH_PROFILE LOAD=MESH_DATA.

The "level before print" steps are the same up to step 3, then BED_MESH_CALIBRATE (with its own tare), BED_MESH_OUTPUT and BED_MESH_PROFILE LOAD=default.

items.title: Stock Z values
items.text:
Adventurer5M.json holds zLevelOffset -3.2342, zProbeOffset 0.04 and zOffset 0.0:

  • zLevelOffset is read as the "level print point Z", used as the saved centre height when the check is configured that way.
  • zOffset (the left extruder's Z offset) appears to be unused: nothing sends it to Klipper.
  • zProbeOffset is the saved live Z adjustment from the print screen, saved as the screen's offset minus its adjustment. Its use at the start of a print was not traced in the decompile. The kiln-os notes say stock sends SET_GCODE_OFFSET Z=<zProbeOffset> MOVE=1 at print start (absolute, replacing the drift offset).
  • At the end of a print stock sends SET_GCODE_OFFSET Z=0 MOVE=1 and BED_MESH_CLEAR.

items.title: kiln-os findings
items.text:
kiln-os (GPLv3) has the same findings, from docs/bed-weighing-board.md (the stock app run in a QEMU sandbox, plus one read on a real AD5X), klipper/extras/ad5x_weight.py and klipper/ad5x.cfg:

  • A real board answered H7 with command H7 ok. 8596371 60 g \r\n (60 g untared, three reads within 1 raw count).
  • The tare runs right before each PROBE_CALIBRATE and before BED_MESH_CALIBRATE.
  • ad5x_weight.py provides [ad5x_weight] (serial, baud, reply_timeout, send_attempts, tare_attempts, tare_tolerance) and the commands WEIGHT_TARE, WEIGHT_READ and WEIGHT_SEND CMD=H....
  • Not confirmed on hardware by kiln-os: that H1 really tares and the probe triggers on contact after it, and what H2 and H3 calibrate.

items.title: Open
items.text:

  • Whether the trigger point stays right without the H1 tare. It triggers, but drift would show as a bad Z or a bad mesh.
  • How stock applies zProbeOffset at the start of a print.
